definition_zh: 重新造林；在被砍伐或烧毁的林地上恢复森林
definition_en: the act or process of planting trees again on land that has lost its forest cover
core_image: 一片被火烧黑的山坡上，人们沿着等高线把一株株幼苗栽进土里，几年后黑色被树冠盖住
scene: 水库上方那片被山火烧黑的山坡上，村民沿着等高线挖坑栽苗，由政府支付工钱。A state programme pays villagers to carry out reforestation on the burnt slopes above the reservoir.
sceneCN: 这里 reforestation 指「在失去森林覆盖的土地上重新植树」（第 1 个义项：在被砍伐或烧毁的林地上恢复森林）；句意为一项州政府计划支付工钱，让村民在水库上方被烧黑的山坡上重新造林。图中可辨识物件：黑色树桩、成排幼苗、等高线土埂、水库水面。

pos.zh: 重新造林；恢复森林（不可数；指具体工程时可用复数）

collocations.zh: 在退化土地上重新造林

forms.label: 复数（指多项工程，较少用）

senses.title: Plant trees where forest was lost
senses.titleCN: 在被砍伐或烧毁的林地上重新植树
senses.definition: to plant trees again on land whose original forest cover has been removed or destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 在原森林被清除或毁坏的土地上再次栽种树木
senses.example: The county began reforestation of the clear-cut hillside in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 县里在春天开始对那片被皆伐的山坡重新造林。
senses.why: re- 'again' plus forest plus -ation 'process' names the act of putting a forest back where one had been.
senses.whyCN: re-「再次」加 forest 与 -ation「过程」，字面就是「把一个曾有过的森林再放回去」。

senses.title: The programme or process as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为一项工程或过程的重新造林
senses.definition: a organized programme, policy or long process of restoring tree cover over an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一区域恢复树木覆盖的有组织计划、政策或长期过程
senses.example: Reforestation in the watershed has run for twelve years without a break.
senses.exampleCN: 该集水区的重新造林已不间断地进行了十二年。
senses.why: the -ation noun can name not only single planting but the whole institutional effort, which is how governments and NGOs use it.
senses.whyCN: -ation 名词不只指一次栽种，也可指整个制度性行动，政府与环保组织正是这样使用。

senses.title: Restore eroded or degraded land
senses.titleCN: 在退化或侵蚀的土地上恢复植被
senses.definition: to establish tree cover on eroded, salinized or exhausted land in order to hold soil and water
senses.definitionCN: 在受侵蚀、盐渍化或耗竭的土地上建立树木覆盖，以保持水土
senses.example: Reforestation of the gullied slopes cut sediment delivery to the river by half.
senses.exampleCN: 在沟蚀坡地上重新造林，使进入河流的泥沙减少了一半。
senses.why: trees are planted here not for timber but as a physical shield, so the word takes on a soil-conservation reading.
senses.whyCN: 此处栽树不为木材，而是当作物理屏障，因此这个词带上了水土保持的含义。

senses.title: Replant after fire
senses.definition: to replant a burned area, often by hand, before grasses and shrubs close the ground
senses.definitionCN: 在草木封住地表之前，对过火地常以人工方式补植
senses.example: After the crown fire, reforestation crews worked the north slope first.
senses.exampleCN: 树冠火过后，造林队先在北坡作业。
senses.why: fire removes both trees and seed source, so the 'again' in re- is literal: people must supply what the forest cannot regrow on its own.
senses.whyCN: 火灾同时带走树木与种源，所以 re- 的「再次」是字面意义：森林无法自行更新，只能由人补上。

senses.title: Restore the native species mix
senses.definition: to replant with species native to the site so that the original community can reassemble
senses.definitionCN: 用当地原生树种补植，使原有群落得以重新组合
senses.example: Their reforestation mixes oak, hazel and rowan instead of a single conifer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的重新造林混种栎、榛与花楸，而非单一针叶树。
senses.why: modern ecology widened reforestation from 'trees' to 'the right trees', because cover alone does not rebuild a forest.
senses.whyCN: 现代生态学把 reforestation 从「有树」扩展为「种对的树」，因为仅有覆盖并不能重建森林。

senses.title: Planting aimed at carbon uptake
senses.definition: tree planting undertaken mainly to absorb atmospheric carbon and meet climate targets
senses.definitionCN: 主要以吸收大气碳、达成气候目标为目的的植树
senses.example: The utility funds reforestation to offset part of its emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电力公司资助重新造林，以抵消部分排放。
senses.why: once forests were valued as carbon stores, reforestation became a measurable climate instrument rather than only a land-repair act.
senses.whyCN: 当森林被当作碳库计价，重新造林就从单纯的土地修复变成可计量的气候工具。

senses.title: Tree planting inside cities
senses.definition: the planting of trees in urban and peri-urban areas for shade, air and storm-water control
senses.definitionCN: 在城市与城郊栽树，以获得遮阴、净化空气与雨水管理
senses.example: Urban reforestation turned six vacant lots into a shaded green corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 城市造林把六块空地变成一条有树荫的绿色廊道。
senses.why: the word's frame is 'land that lost forest', and paved districts qualify: they too once held trees.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的框架是「失去森林的土地」，铺满水泥的城区同样符合：那里也曾有树。

senses.title: Commercial plantation replanting
senses.titleCN: 商业人工林的重新种植
senses.definition: the replanting of a harvested timber stand with fast-growing trees for later cutting
senses.definitionCN: 在采伐后的林分补种速生树，以备将来再次采伐
senses.example: Company reforestation follows each harvest with a uniform pine seedling.
senses.exampleCN: 公司每次采伐后都用统一的松树苗重新造林。
senses.why: industry keeps the word but narrows it to 'restock the crop', which can conflict with the ecological reading.
senses.whyCN: 林业产业保留这个词，却把它窄化为「补足作物」，这可能与生态义相冲突。

intro.en: Reforestation joins Latin-derived forest with the prefix re- 'again' and the noun suffix -ation; the compound itself is a modern English formation, not a Latin word.
intro.cn: reforestation 由拉丁来源的 forest 加上前缀 re-「再次」与名词后缀 -ation 构成；这个复合词本身是近代英语新造，并非拉丁词。

items.en: Forest goes back to Medieval Latin forestis (silva), 'woodland outside the walls', from foris 'outside, out of doors'. The exact legal origin is still debated.
items.cn: forest 可上溯到中世纪拉丁 forestis（silva）「墙外的林地」，来自 foris「在外面、户外」。其确切的法律来源仍有争论。

items.en: Old French forest passed the word into Middle English, where it first named a royal hunting preserve before naming any large wood.
items.cn: 古法语 forest 把这个词带进中古英语，最初指王室猎场，之后才泛指大片树林。

items.en: By the sixteenth century forest meant simply a large area thickly covered with trees, and the verb forest 'to plant with trees' followed.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，forest 已直接指树木茂密的大片土地，动词 forest「植树于」也随之出现。

items.en: Nineteenth-century forestry added re- 'again' and -ation 'process' to forest, producing a transparent English compound for replanting after cutting.
items.cn: 19 世纪的林业用语把 re-「再次」与 -ation「过程」加到 forest 上，造出这个结构透明的英语复合词，指采伐后的补植。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first recorded use of reforestation is not securely dated, and whether forestis derives from foris 'outside' or from a Germanic root remains a reconstruction rather than a settled fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定：reforestation 的最早书证年代没有可靠定论；forestis 究竟出自 foris「外面」还是日耳曼词根，也只是重构，并非定论。

note.en: Group one collects the -forestation compounds that differ only by prefix; group two collects words for bringing vegetation back.
note.cn: 第一组是只靠前缀区分的 -forestation 复合词；第二组是表示「让植被回来」的近义词。

entries.definition: Ad- 'to' plus forest: planting trees on land that has not recently carried forest, such as bare moor or former farmland.
entries.definitionCN: ad-「朝向」加 forest：在近期没有森林的土地上植树，如光秃荒原或退耕地。

entries.definition: De- 'away, remove' plus forest: clearing trees permanently, the exact reverse of reforestation.
entries.definitionCN: de-「去除」加 forest：永久清除树木，与 reforestation 正好相反。

entries.definition: A British variant that doubles the 'again' idea with re- and ad-; it is largely interchangeable but less common internationally.
entries.definitionCN: 英式变体，用 re- 与 ad- 重复表达「再次」；大体可互换，但国际上较少用。

entries.definition: The bare noun for tree planting without saying whether the land was previously wooded.
entries.definitionCN: 不带前缀的统称，只说植树，不说明该地原本是否有林。

entries.definition: Bringing an entire ecosystem back toward its former structure; reforestation may be only one step in it.
entries.definitionCN: 使整个生态系统回到原有结构；重新造林可能只是其中一步。

entries.definition: Putting plants back into the ground, often in a garden or a small site; it says nothing about a forest.
entries.definitionCN: 把植物重新栽回土里，常用于花园或小块地，并不涉及森林。

entries.definition: Re-establishing any vegetation, including grasses and shrubs, not necessarily trees.
entries.definitionCN: 重建任何植被，包括草与灌木，不一定有树。

entries.definition: Forest renewal from seed or sprouts without planting; reforestation usually implies human planting.
entries.definitionCN: 森林靠种子或萌蘖自行更新；reforestation 通常意味着人工栽植。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + forest + -ation 'process': putting a forest back.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ forest + -ation「过程」：把森林放回去。

normal.en: The family runs forest, reforest, reforestation, afforestation, deforestation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 forest、reforest、reforestation、afforestation、deforestation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: reforestation project, large-scale reforestation, reforestation of degraded land.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：重新造林项目、大规模重新造林、退化土地上的重新造林。

normal.en: The prefix re- is the key: afforestation has no 'again', deforestation takes away.
normal.cn: 关键在前缀：afforestation 没有「再次」，deforestation 则是拿走。

normal.en: The figure is a burned slope refilled with seedlings along contour lines.
normal.cn: 意象是被烧黑的山坡上沿等高线补满幼苗。

abstract.en: Think of a page erased and then written over with the same story in a slower hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被擦掉，又用更慢的笔迹把同一个故事重新写上。

abstract.en: Think of a lung regrowing its fine branches after smoke has stripped them.
abstract.cn: 想象肺叶被烟熏掉细枝后，又一点点长回分支。

abstract.en: Think of a debt repaid not in one sum but tree by tree over decades.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔债不是一次还清，而是几十年里一棵树一棵树地偿还。

examples.en: Reforestation of the catchment began after the 1998 floods.
examples.cn: 1998 年洪水之后，该集水区开始重新造林。

examples.en: The charity trains farmers in low-cost reforestation.
examples.cn: 该慈善机构培训农民掌握低成本的重新造林方法。

examples.en: Without reforestation, the bare slope will keep sliding into the road.
examples.cn: 若不重新造林，那片裸露坡地会不断塌到路上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ forest（森林）+ ation（动作）」——再把森林种回去 → 重新造林

root: 拉丁 foris「外面」→ 中世纪拉丁 forestis (silva)「墙外林地」→ 古法语 forest → 英语 forest；再加 re-「再次」与 -ation「过程」构成英语新词。forestis 的更深来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one repair: a piece of land has lost its trees, and people put them back, whether the aim is soil, habitat, carbon, shade or timber.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次修补展开：一块土地失去了树，人把树放回去，目的可以是水土、栖息地、碳、遮阴或木材。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black burn scar on a hillside being steadily covered by young trees.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡上一道黑色的火烧痕，正被幼树一点点盖住。

branches.en: STARTING POINT: whether the loss came from axes or fire, the first move is to put seedlings in the ground.
branches.cn: 起点：无论失去森林的原因是斧头还是火，第一步都是把苗栽进土里。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: one planting becomes a programme with budgets, crews and years.
branches.cn: 制度化：一次栽种变成有预算、有队伍、跨年份的计划。

branches.en: LAND REPAIR: trees are planted as a shield for soil, water and city air.
branches.cn: 土地修复：树被当作盾牌，护住土壤、水源与城市空气。

branches.en: ECOLOGICAL VALUE: the right mix rebuilds a community, and the growing wood stores carbon.
branches.cn: 生态价值：正确的树种组合重建群落，长出的木材储存碳。

branches.en: PRODUCTION: the same act can be narrowed to restocking a timber crop.
branches.cn: 生产：同一个动作也可被窄化为补足木材作物。

intro.en: Reforestation is built from an English noun and two productive affixes, so each piece can be read separately.
intro.cn: reforestation 由一个英语名词与两个能产后缀、前缀构成，各部分是读得出来的。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is foris 'outside', which produced forestis; re- and -ation are affixes that English attaches freely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 foris「外面」，它产生 forestis；re- 与 -ation 是英语可自由附加的缀。

items.example: The prefix says the forest is being put back.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀说明森林正被放回去。

items.example: The forest above the village was cut in the 1980s.
items.exampleCN: 村子上方的森林在 1980 年代被砍伐。

items.meaning: the act, process or result of doing
items.example: The suffix turns the verb reforest into the name of a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词 reforest 变成过程之名。

items.example: Crews reforest the slope by hand.
items.exampleCN: 工人以人工方式在这片坡地重新造林。

items.example: Afforestation converted the moor into conifer plantation.
items.exampleCN: 造林把荒原变成了针叶林。

items.example: Deforestation upstream worsened the flooding.
items.exampleCN: 上游的毁林加重了洪水。

items.example: Forestation has no prefix because it picks no starting point.
items.exampleCN: forestation 不带前缀，因为它不指定起点。

items.example: The reforested catchment now holds water longer.
items.exampleCN: 已重新造林的集水区现在能更久地蓄住水。

definition_zh: 林地；树木覆盖的土地；（英）成片小树林；疏林
definition_en: land covered with trees, usually smaller or more open than a full forest
core_image: 一片不过几百步宽的榛树林，林下有风信子，林外就是麦田，树冠把两种土地分开
scene: 五月初，这片矮林刚被砍过一茬，林下开满风信子，是庄园里物种最丰富的生境之一。In early May the hazel coppice and bluebells make this woodland one of the richest habitats on the estate.
sceneCN: 这里 woodland 指「树木覆盖的成片土地」（第 1 个义项：以树木为主的陆地区域）；句意为五月初这茬矮林与风信子使这片林地成为庄园里最丰富的生境之一。图中可辨识物件：榛树萌条、风信子花丛、林缘麦田、林下落叶层。

pos.zh: 林地；小树林；疏林（可数或不可数）
林地的；林栖的（多作定语）

collocations.zh: 古老林地（长期连续有林）

derivatives.zh: 林居者；林地居民（较少用）

senses.title: Land covered with trees
senses.definition: an area of land whose main cover is trees, generally smaller than a forest and often bounded by fields
senses.definitionCN: 以树木为主要覆盖的陆地区域，通常比森林小，常与农田相接
senses.example: A narrow woodland separates the village from the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 一片狭长林地把村庄与公路隔开。
senses.why: woodland is literally 'wood-land', a compound that names land by what grows on it rather than by ownership or size.
senses.whyCN: woodland 字面就是「长树的土地」，这个复合词按地表长什么来命名，而不按所有权或面积。

senses.title: A managed wood in Britain
senses.definition: a small wood that is actively managed, often by coppicing or thinning, as a land-use category
senses.definitionCN: 经积极经营的小片树林，常行矮林作业或疏伐，作为土地用途类别
senses.example: The trust owns forty hectares of woodland under a coppice rotation.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托拥有四十公顷按矮林轮伐经营的林地。
senses.why: British land-use vocabulary separates woodland from forest, because a forest there is often a large open hunting area rather than a closed wood.
senses.whyCN: 英国土地用途术语把 woodland 与 forest 分开，因为那里的 forest 常指大片开阔猎场，而非密闭树林。

senses.title: Open woodland with scattered canopy
senses.definition: a tree community whose crowns do not close, so that grass or heath grows between the trunks
senses.definitionCN: 树冠不闭合的树木群落，树干之间长着草或灌丛
senses.example: Open woodland lets light reach the grass layer all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 疏林让阳光整个夏天都能照到草层。
senses.why: ecology uses woodland as a structural term, and the open type sits between grassland and closed forest.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把 woodland 当作结构术语，疏林型正好位于草地与密闭森林之间。

senses.title: Habitat with layered vegetation
senses.titleCN: 具有垂直层次的林地生境
senses.definition: a habitat whose canopy, shrub layer and litter support distinct groups of animals and plants
senses.definitionCN: 由树冠层、灌木层与落叶层构成、供养不同动植物类群的生境
senses.example: The woodland shelters warblers in the canopy and beetles in the litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这片林地为树冠层的莺与落叶层的甲虫提供庇护。
senses.why: once woodland is seen as a place rather than a crop, it becomes a habitat whose value lies in its layers.
senses.whyCN: 当 woodland 被视为一个地方而非作物，它就成了生境，其价值在于层次。

senses.title: Ancient woodland with long continuity
senses.titleCN: 长期连续有林的古老林地
senses.definition: woodland that has been continuously wooded since at least 1600, and so preserves old soil and plant communities
senses.definitionCN: 至少自 1600 年起持续有林、因而保存古老土壤与植物群落的林地
senses.example: Ancient woodland indicators such as wild garlic cover the slope.
senses.exampleCN: 野蒜等古老林地指示植物覆盖着这片坡地。
senses.why: continuity, not age of individual trees, defines the type: a wood can be cut many times and still be ancient.
senses.whyCN: 定义这个类型的是连续性而非单株树龄：一片林子可被反复采伐，仍算古老林地。

senses.title: Woodland edge as a transition
senses.definition: the boundary zone where woodland meets field or clearing, richer in light and in species than either side
senses.definitionCN: 林地与田野或空地相接的边界带，光照与物种都比两侧更丰富
senses.example: Butterflies concentrate along the sunny woodland edge.
senses.exampleCN: 蝴蝶聚集在向阳的林缘。
senses.why: the compound's 'land' part becomes visible here: woodland is a patch with a boundary, and the boundary is itself a habitat.
senses.whyCN: 这里显出复合词中 land 的一面：林地是有边界的地块，而边界本身也是生境。

senses.title: Newly created woodland
senses.definition: trees planted on former farmland or bare ground with the declared aim of forming woodland
senses.definitionCN: 在退耕地或裸地上植树，目标明确为形成林地
senses.example: Woodland creation on the upper fields has doubled tree cover in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 在上部农田新造林地，使树木覆盖在十年内翻倍。
senses.why: the word can look forward as well as backward: land becomes woodland at the moment the planting scheme is registered.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能朝前看：当造林方案登记之时，那块地就被算作林地。

senses.title: Woodland as a source of woodfuel
senses.definition: woodland valued for the regular supply of logs, poles and charcoal it yields under a cutting cycle
senses.definitionCN: 因按采伐周期稳定产出原木、杆材与木炭而受重视的林地
senses.example: The woodland heats three cottages from a single winter cut.
senses.exampleCN: 这片林地一次冬季采伐就能供三座农舍取暖。
senses.why: the oldest use of a wood was to be cut on rotation, and this productive reading still attaches to woodland in rural economies.
senses.whyCN: 树林最古老的用途就是轮期采伐，这一生产性含义在乡村经济中仍附着于 woodland。

intro.en: Woodland is a native English compound of wood and land, both Old English words of Germanic origin, so it has no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: woodland 是 wood 与 land 构成的英语本族复合词，两者都是日耳曼来源的古英语词，因此没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Wudu meant 'wood, tree, forest'. Its Germanic source is usually reconstructed as *widuz, but the further Indo-European connections are not settled.
items.cn: wudu 意为「木材、树、森林」。其日耳曼来源通常重构为 *widuz，更远的印欧语联系尚无定论。

items.en: Land meant 'ground, soil, territory'. Germanic *landam is reconstructed, but its pre-Germanic origin is uncertain.
items.cn: land 意为「地面、土壤、领土」。日耳曼语 *landam 属重构形式，其在日耳曼语之前的来源不确定。

items.en: The compound is recorded in Middle English, naming ground grown with trees rather than the trees themselves.
items.cn: 这个复合词见于中古英语，指长着树木的地面，而非树木本身。

items.en: Modern forestry fixed woodland as a category distinct from forest, especially in Britain, where forest often names an old royal hunting area.
items.cn: 现代林业把 woodland 固定为与 forest 不同的类别，在英国尤其如此，因为那里的 forest 常指旧日王室猎场。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first date of the compound is not precisely recorded, and the deeper roots of both wudu and land are reconstructions rather than attested forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个复合词的最早年代没有精确书证；wudu 与 land 的更深词根均属重构，并非有文献的形式。

note.en: Group one separates the wood-words by size and management; group two gives true synonyms for a stand of trees.
note.cn: 第一组按面积与经营方式区分几个 wood 系词；第二组是「一片树林」的真正近义词。

entries.definition: A small area of trees, or the material cut from them; in British English a wood is typically smaller than a woodland.
entries.definitionCN: 小片树林，或由其砍出的木材；英式英语中 wood 通常比 woodland 更小。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'covered with trees', used of hills or land, not a noun for the place itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「树木覆盖的」，用于山丘或土地，不是地点名词。

entries.definition: A North American term for a small privately owned stand of trees managed for fuel and fence posts.
entries.definitionCN: 北美用语，指私有小片树林，经营薪材与篱柱。

entries.definition: A larger, denser or legally designated wooded area; historically a royal hunting ground, which is why British usage differs.
entries.definitionCN: 更大、更密或依法划定的林区；历史上指王室猎场，这正是英式用法差异的由来。

entries.definition: A small group of trees, often of one kind and often in open ground; it stresses cluster, not area.
entries.definitionCN: 一小群树，常为同一树种，多生于开阔地；强调成簇，不强调面积。

entries.definition: A small wood grown for periodic cutting, from Old French copeiz; it names a working wood rather than any tree-covered land.
entries.definitionCN: 为定期采伐而育的小树林，来自古法语 copeiz；指作业林，而非任意林地。

entries.definition: Australian land dominated by shrubs and scattered trees; the cover is lower and drier than woodland.
entries.definitionCN: 澳洲以灌木与散生树为主的土地；覆盖比林地更低更干。

entries.definition: Forest land valued for the timber it can yield; it is an economic label, not an ecological one.
entries.definitionCN: 以可产木材为价值的林地；是经济标签，不是生态分类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: wood + land: land whose crop is trees.
normal.cn: wood + land：以树为作物的土地。

normal.en: The family runs wood, wooded, woody, woodlot, woodland.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 wood、wooded、woody、woodlot、woodland。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: ancient woodland, open woodland, woodland edge, woodland creation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：古老林地、疏林、林缘、新造林地。

normal.en: British usage keeps woodland smaller than forest; American usage often treats them alike.
normal.cn: 英式用法中 woodland 比 forest 小；美式用法常不加区分。

normal.en: The image is a narrow wood with a field on one side and a road on the other.
normal.cn: 意象是一片窄林，一边是麦田，一边是公路。

abstract.en: Think of a green room whose walls are trunks and whose ceiling is leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一间绿色的屋子，墙是树干，顶是叶子。

abstract.en: Think of a shadow that stays in one place while the fields around it are cut and sown.
abstract.cn: 想象一片停在原处的阴影，周围的田地不断被收割与播种。

abstract.en: Think of a bookshelf with three shelves: canopy, shrub, litter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个三层书架：树冠层、灌木层、落叶层。

examples.en: The path runs through a hazel woodland that is cut every seventh winter.
examples.cn: 小路穿过一片每七个冬季采伐一次的榛树林。

examples.en: Ancient woodland soils store carbon that a new plantation cannot quickly replace.
examples.cn: 古老林地的土壤储存着新人工林无法迅速替代的碳。

examples.en: Woodland birds declined after the hedges were removed.
examples.cn: 树篱被清除后，林栖鸟类减少了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wood（木头/树林）+ land（土地）」——长满树的土地 → 林地

root: 古英语 wudu「木材、树、森林」+ land「土地、地面」。二者均属日耳曼语来源（*widuz、*landam 为重构形式），更深词源不确定；无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the plain fact of trees on land to the many ways such land is managed, measured, inhabited and cut.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「土地上有树」这一朴素事实，走向这类土地被经营、计量、栖息与采伐的各种方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bounded patch of trees with fields pressing against its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片有边界的树地，田地紧贴着它的边缘。

branches.en: THE PATCH: first a piece of land with trees, then a piece someone actually works.
branches.cn: 地块：先是有树的一片地，再是有人实际经营的一片地。

branches.en: LIGHT: when crowns fail to close, grass enters and the type becomes open woodland.
branches.cn: 光：树冠不闭合时草层进入，类型就成了疏林。

branches.en: LAYERS AND BORDER: habitat value sits in canopy, shrub and litter, and peaks at the sunny edge.
branches.cn: 层次与边界：生境价值在树冠、灌木与落叶层中，并在向阳林缘达到高峰。

branches.en: TIME: a wood can be cut again and again and still be ancient if the ground never cleared.
branches.cn: 时间：只要地面未被彻底清除，林子可反复采伐，仍属古老林地。

branches.en: FUTURE AND YIELD: land can be made woodland, and woodland can be made fuel.
branches.cn: 未来与产出：土地可被造成林地，林地也可被变成燃料。

intro.en: Woodland is a native compound, so its parts are two free English words rather than a prefix and a root.
intro.cn: woodland 是本族复合词，其组成部分是两个独立的英语单词，而不是前缀加词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in woodland; both halves are Germanic, so the Latin entry list is left empty rather than filled with invented relatives.
latinIntro.cn: woodland 中没有拉丁成分；两半都属日耳曼语，因此拉丁词条留空，而不编造同族词。

items.example: The old wood was cut for charcoal.
items.exampleCN: 那片老树林被砍去烧炭。

items.example: The land east of the stream is wet all year.
items.exampleCN: 溪流以东的土地终年潮湿。

items.example: The woodland stops at the fence.
items.exampleCN: 林地在栅栏处止住。

items.example: A wooded ridge hides the quarry.
items.exampleCN: 一道长满树的岭遮住了采石场。

items.example: Woody stems survive the winter above ground.
items.exampleCN: 木质茎能在地面上越冬。

items.meaning: a small private stand of trees
items.example: He cuts one row of his woodlot each year.
items.exampleCN: 他每年在自己那片小树林里砍一行。

items.meaning: one who lives in or works a wood
items.example: The woodlander knows which oaks are ready.
items.exampleCN: 林居者知道哪些栎树可以采了。

items.meaning: of or belonging to a wood
items.example: Woodland birds need the shrub layer.
items.exampleCN: 林栖鸟类需要灌木层。

definition_zh: 灌木；灌木丛；（园艺）花灌木；灌木层；果味糖浆饮（旧义，另源）
definition_en: a woody plant smaller than a tree, usually with several stems growing from the base
core_image: 一株不到腰高的木本植物，从同一个基部抽出三根细茎，旁边高树的树干已经枯死
scene: 同一基部抽出三根细茎的矮灌木，在高树枯死的地方仍然活着。A low shrub with three stems from the same base survived where the taller trees had died.
sceneCN: 这里 shrub 指「低于乔木、通常自基部分出多根茎的木本植物」（第 1 个义项：小型多茎木本植物）；句意为同一基部抽出三根茎的矮灌木，在高树枯死之处存活下来。图中可辨识物件：三根细茎、共同基部、枯死的高树干、裸露地面。

pos.zh: 灌木；灌木丛（可数；集合义不可数）
果味糖浆饮（加醋或酒，18 世纪旧义，词源不同）

forms.label: 形容词（灌木状的；多灌木的）
名词（灌木丛；灌木栽植区）

derivatives.zh: 半灌木（基部木质、上部草质）

senses.title: A small multi-stemmed woody plant
senses.definition: a woody plant that stays low and usually sends up several stems from the same base instead of one trunk
senses.definitionCN: 一种低矮的木本植物，通常自同一基部长出多根茎，而非单一下干
senses.example: A low shrub with three stems from the same base survived the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 同一基部抽出三根茎的矮灌木熬过了干旱。
senses.why: the word's core is lowness plus woodiness: it is not a small tree because it branches at the ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是「低矮」加「木质」：它不是小树，因为它在贴地处就分叉。

senses.title: Shrubs planted as a garden mass
senses.titleCN: 庭园中成片栽植的灌木
senses.definition: a group or mass of low woody plants grown together for cover, flowers or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 成片栽植的低矮木本植物，用于遮蔽、观花或作边界
senses.example: The gardener cut the shrub back hard after flowering.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁在花后把这丛灌木重剪了一遍。
senses.why: in garden talk the countable plant and the uncountable mass blur, so 'the shrub' can mean the whole bed.
senses.whyCN: 在园艺口语中，单株与成片混在一起，因此这个说法也可指整片花坛。

senses.title: The botanical growth form
senses.titleCN: 植物学上的灌木生长型
senses.definition: a growth form defined by persistent woody stems branching near ground level and a mature height well below the tree layer
senses.definitionCN: 一种生长型：具宿存木质茎、贴近地面分枝，成熟高度远低于乔木层
senses.example: The flora keys out the shrub by its basal branching, not by its height alone.
senses.exampleCN: 这本植物志以基部分枝、而非单以高度来检索灌木。
senses.why: botany needs a form category between herb and tree, and shrub names exactly that middle.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要一个介于草本与乔木之间的形态类别，shrub 正指这个中间层。

senses.title: A flowering ornamental shrub
senses.definition: a woody plant chosen and pruned mainly for showy flowers or coloured foliage in a garden
senses.definitionCN: 主要因花艳或叶色而在庭园中被选用、修剪的木本植物
senses.example: A pink flowering shrub anchors the corner of the border.
senses.exampleCN: 一株开粉花的灌木压住花坛转角。
senses.why: horticulture shifted the emphasis from wild form to cultivated display, so shrub came to mean a planted ornament.
senses.whyCN: 园艺学把重点从野生形态移到栽培展示，于是 shrub 也指栽下的观赏植物。

senses.title: The shrub layer of a forest
senses.definition: the vertical layer of woody plants between the herb layer and the tree canopy
senses.definitionCN: 位于草本层与乔木树冠之间的木本植物层
senses.example: Deer browsing has stripped the shrub layer from the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿的啃食已把这片林子的灌木层剥光。
senses.why: in ecology a single plant gives its name to a whole stratum, because that layer is made of such plants.
senses.whyCN: 生态学中用单株植物之名指整个层，因为该层正是由这类植物构成。

senses.title: A dryland or scrub shrub
senses.definition: a tough, often thorny or waxy-leaved woody plant that dominates dry scrub and semi-desert
senses.definitionCN: 常带刺或具蜡质叶的耐旱木本植物，在干旱灌丛与半荒漠中占优势
senses.example: Salt-tolerant shrubs line the dry lake bed.
senses.exampleCN: 耐盐灌木沿干涸湖床排成一线。
senses.why: where trees cannot hold, shrubs become the dominant cover, so the word doubles as a landscape label.
senses.whyCN: 在乔木立不住的地方，灌木成为主要覆盖，于是这个词也兼作景观标签。

senses.title: Woody encroachment on open land
senses.definition: the spread of woody plants into grassland or pasture, often seen as degradation
senses.definitionCN: 木本植物向草地或牧场扩张，常被视为退化
senses.example: Unchecked grazing let shrub take over the lower pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 放牧失控让灌木占据了低处牧场。
senses.why: a plant name turns into a process name when the plant's spread changes what the land is.
senses.whyCN: 当某种植物的扩张改变了土地性质，植物名就变成了过程名。

senses.title: The old fruit-syrup drink
senses.titleCN: 旧时的果味糖浆饮（另源）
senses.definition: a drink made from fruit juice, sugar and vinegar or rum, popular in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries
senses.definitionCN: 由果汁、糖与醋或朗姆酒调成的饮品，在 18 至 19 世纪流行
senses.example: A jug of raspberry shrub stood cooling on the sill.
senses.exampleCN: 一罐覆盆子糖浆饮放在窗台上晾凉。
senses.why: this is a homonym, not a development of the plant sense: it comes through Arabic sharab 'a drink'.
senses.whyCN: 这是同形异源词，并非植物义的引申：它经阿拉伯语 sharab「饮料」而来。

intro.en: Shrub 'low woody plant' is a Germanic word of uncertain deeper origin; shrub 'fruit drink' is an unrelated homonym from Arabic.
intro.cn: shrub「低矮木本植物」是日耳曼词，更深来源不确定；shrub「果汁饮」则是来自阿拉伯语的不相关同形词。

items.en: Old English scrybb named brushwood and low woody growth. The form is recorded chiefly in glosses, so its early history is thin.
items.cn: 古英语 scrybb 指柴枝与低矮木本植物。该形式主要见于注释文献，早期历史材料很少。

items.en: The word matches North Frisian skrobb 'brushwood' and West Flemish schrobbe 'climbing vetch', which points to a North Sea Germanic stock.
items.cn: 这个词与北弗里斯兰语 skrobb「柴枝」、西佛兰德语 schrobbe「野豌豆」相合，指向北海日耳曼语来源。

items.en: Middle English shrub kept both the plant and the cut-brushwood readings, and the plant sense gradually dominated.
items.cn: 中古英语 shrub 同时保留「植物」与「砍下的柴枝」两义，后来植物义逐渐占主导。

items.en: The drink shrub entered English in the eighteenth century through Arabic sharab 'a drink' (compare sherbet and syrup), a completely separate line.
items.cn: 指饮品的 shrub 于 18 世纪经阿拉伯语 sharab「饮料」进入英语（参较 sherbet 与 syrup），是完全独立的一线。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): no Germanic etymon beyond the North Sea forms is attested, and the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction; the first English citation of the plant sense is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：除北海诸语形式外没有更早的日耳曼语书证，其日耳曼语之前的词根属重构；植物义的最早英语书证年代也不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates shrub from its closest woody-plant neighbours; group two separates the vegetation words that are not single plants.
note.cn: 第一组把 shrub 与最接近的木本植物词分开；第二组区分那些指植被而非单株的词。

entries.definition: A general word for a low woody plant, often wild and rounded; shrub is the more technical and garden term.
entries.definitionCN: 低矮木本植物的通称，常指野生、团状者；shrub 更技术化，也更常用于园艺。

entries.definition: Low woody vegetation as a cover type, often stunted or thorny; it rarely names a single plant.
entries.definitionCN: 作为覆盖类型的低矮木本植被，常矮小或多刺；很少指单株植物。

entries.definition: A young tree with a single stem; it differs from a shrub in having one trunk that will grow tall.
entries.definitionCN: 单茎的幼树；与灌木的区别在于只有一根将来会长高的主干。

entries.definition: A plant woody only at the base and herbaceous above, so it dies back partly each winter.
entries.definitionCN: 仅基部木质、上部草质的植物，每年冬季部分枯死。

entries.definition: A planted area of shrubs, usually in a garden or park; it names the bed, not the species.
entries.definitionCN: 庭园或公园中成片栽植的灌木区；指花坛，不指物种。

entries.definition: The low plants growing beneath a forest canopy, including herbs and shrubs; broader than shrub.
entries.definitionCN: 林冠下生长的低矮植物，含草本与灌木；范围比 shrub 宽。

entries.definition: A line of shrubs planted and clipped as a barrier; the shrubs are means, the barrier is the point.
entries.definitionCN: 成行栽植并修剪作屏障的灌木；灌木是手段，屏障才是目的。

entries.definition: A dense stand of shrubs or small trees hard to walk through; it stresses impenetrability.
entries.definitionCN: 难以穿行的密集灌木或小树丛；强调难以通过。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One base, many stems: that is the difference between a shrub and a tree.
normal.cn: 一个基部、多根茎：这就是灌木与乔木的区别。

normal.en: The family runs shrub, shrubby, shrubbery, shrubland, subshrub.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 shrub、shrubby、shrubbery、shrubland、subshrub。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: flowering shrub, evergreen shrub, shrub layer, desert shrub.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：花灌木、常绿灌木、灌木层、荒漠灌木。

normal.en: Ecology names a whole layer after the plant: the shrub layer.
normal.cn: 生态学以这种植物之名为整层命名：灌木层。

normal.en: The homonym warning: the fruit drink comes from Arabic, not from the plant.
normal.cn: 同形异源提醒：果汁饮来自阿拉伯语，与植物无关。

abstract.en: Think of a hand that never grew one wrist but five fingers straight from the palm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手没有手腕，五根手指直接从掌心长出。

abstract.en: Think of a low wall that keeps growing back after every cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵矮墙，每次被砍后都重新长回。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd of short people holding a tall forest up from below.
abstract.cn: 想象一群矮个子在下面把高处的森林托住。

examples.en: Goats will eat almost any shrub before they touch the grass.
examples.cn: 山羊几乎先吃光任何灌木，才去碰草。

examples.en: The shrub layer recovered two years after the fire.
examples.cn: 火灾两年后灌木层恢复了。

examples.en: A single shrub can anchor a whole dune.
examples.cn: 一株灌木就能固定整座沙丘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「shrub」读音像「刷布」——矮矮一丛，像刷子一样贴地散开 → 灌木

root: 古英语 scrybb「柴枝、低矮木本植物」，与北弗里斯兰语 skrobb、西佛兰德语 schrobbe 同源，属北海日耳曼语一线；更深词根不确定。指饮品的 shrub 另出阿拉伯语 sharab。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one plant: it grows low and many-stemmed, fills gardens and forest layers, takes over dry ground, and finally shares its spelling with an unrelated drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一株植物展开：它低矮多茎，填满庭园与森林层次，占据干旱地，最后又与一种无关的饮料共用拼写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one root crown sending up several thin stems instead of a single trunk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个根颈抽出几根细茎，而不是一根主干。

branches.en: FORM: lowness and basal branching define the plant both in common speech and in botany.
branches.cn: 形态：低矮与基部分枝，在日常语与植物学中都定义这种植物。

branches.en: GARDEN: the plant becomes an ornamental mass chosen for flower and boundary.
branches.cn: 庭园：这种植物成为按花与边界选用的观赏群体。

branches.en: STRATUM: in a wood the same plant gives its name to a whole layer.
branches.cn: 层次：在林中，同一种植物为整个层命名。

branches.en: DRY LAND: where trees fail, shrubs dominate, and their spread can count as degradation.
branches.cn: 旱地：乔木立不住时灌木占优，其扩张可算作退化。

branches.en: HOMONYM: the drink is a separate Arabic loan, so the two meanings must not be linked.
branches.cn: 同形异源：饮料是独立的阿拉伯语借词，两义不可串联。

intro.en: Shrub is a free root that takes several suffixes, producing a compact family of plant and landscape words.
intro.cn: shrub 是自由词根，可接若干后缀，形成一组紧凑的植物与景观词族。

latinIntro.en: Shrub has no Latin ancestor; the only Latin-looking item here, sub-, is a prefix borrowed into English word formation, not evidence of a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: shrub 没有拉丁语祖先；此处唯一像拉丁语的 sub- 是英语构词借用的前缀，不能当作拉丁词根的证据。

items.example: The shrub regrew from the cut stems.
items.exampleCN: 这株灌木从被砍的茎上重新长出。

items.meaning: like a shrub; full of shrubs
items.example: The shrubby slope holds the soil.
items.exampleCN: 长满灌木的坡地能保住土壤。

items.example: A clipped shrubbery hides the wall.
items.exampleCN: 一片修剪过的灌木丛遮住了墙。

items.example: Shrubland replaced the overgrazed pasture.
items.exampleCN: 灌木林地取代了过牧的牧场。

items.meaning: a plant woody only at the base
items.example: Lavender is often grown as a subshrub.
items.exampleCN: 薰衣草常被当作半灌木栽培。

items.example: The sprayed verge was almost shrubless.
items.exampleCN: 喷过药的路边几乎没有灌木。

items.meaning: where shrubs are the main cover
items.example: A shrub-dominated community followed the fire.
items.exampleCN: 火灾后形成以灌木为主的群落。

items.example: Shrub-steppe supports sagebrush and bunchgrass.
items.exampleCN: 灌木草原上长着山艾与丛生禾草。

definition_zh: 灌木林地；以灌木为主要覆盖的土地；灌丛植被类型
definition_en: land whose dominant vegetation is shrubs rather than trees or grasses
core_image: 一片坡度不大的坡地，齐腰高的灌木连成片，中间只夹着几条草缝，远处没有一棵高树
scene: 火烧过后的坡地，五年之内就长成齐腰高的灌丛，草挤不进去，高树也还没回来。After the fire the slope became shrubland within five years, too dense for grass but too low for forest.
sceneCN: 这里 shrubland 指「以灌木为主要覆盖的土地」（第 1 个义项：灌木占优势的植被类型）；句意为火烧之后五年内坡地变成灌丛，密得草进不来，又低得算不上森林。图中可辨识物件：连片灌木、草缝、黑色残桩、远处无高树的天际线。

pos.zh: 灌木林地；灌丛（可数或不可数）

senses.title: Vegetation dominated by shrubs
senses.titleCN: 以灌木为主的植被类型
senses.definition: a plant community in which shrubs form the main cover and trees are absent or too sparse to close a canopy
senses.definitionCN: 以灌木构成主要覆盖、乔木缺失或稀疏到无法闭合树冠的植物群落
senses.example: The reserve protects a rare dwarf shrubland on thin soil.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区守护着薄土上一种稀有的矮灌丛。
senses.why: shrub plus land names a cover type by its dominant growth form, the same way grassland is named by grass.
senses.whyCN: shrub 加 land 按优势生长型给覆盖类型命名，正如 grassland 按草命名。

senses.title: The land area itself
senses.definition: a tract of ground whose cover is shrubs, considered as a unit of property or management
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖为灌木的一片土地，作为产权或经营单元来看待
senses.example: They fenced the shrubland off from the grazing allotment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把这片灌丛地与放牧区用围栏隔开。
senses.why: adding land shifts attention from the plants to the ground they occupy, which is what maps and leases need.
senses.whyCN: 加上 land 后，注意力从植物转到它们占据的地面，这正是地图与租约所需要的。

senses.title: A stage after disturbance
senses.definition: an intermediate seral stage in which shrubs colonize a burned, cleared or abandoned site before trees take over
senses.definitionCN: 火烧、清除或弃耕之后，灌木先占据、乔木随后接管的中间演替阶段
senses.example: Shrubland persisted for a decade before the pines seeded in.
senses.exampleCN: 灌丛持续了十年，松树才播种进来。
senses.why: ecology reads shrubland as a phase as well as a place, because shrub cover is often temporary.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把灌丛既看作地点也看作阶段，因为灌木覆盖常常是暂时的。

senses.title: Mediterranean-type shrubland
senses.definition: dense evergreen scrub of winter-wet, summer-dry regions, known as maquis, chaparral or garrigue
senses.definitionCN: 冬雨夏旱地区常绿密灌丛，分别称 maquis、chaparral 或 garrigue
senses.example: Mediterranean shrubland smells of thyme after rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后地中海灌丛满是百里香的气味。
senses.why: the type is defined by climate rather than by continent, so one word covers several regional names.
senses.whyCN: 这一类型按气候而非按大洲定义，因此一个词覆盖数个地区名称。

senses.title: Semi-arid and desert shrubland
senses.definition: sparse, drought-adapted shrub cover on dry soils where grass growth is limited by rainfall
senses.definitionCN: 干旱土壤上稀疏、耐旱的灌木覆盖，草本生长受降水限制
senses.example: Saltbush shrubland carries sheep through the dry season.
senses.exampleCN: 盐灌木灌丛能让羊群度过旱季。
senses.why: in dry country shrubland is not a transition but a stable climax, which changes how it should be managed.
senses.whyCN: 在干旱地区，灌丛不是过渡而是稳定顶极，这改变了经营方式。

senses.title: Wildlife habitat in shrub cover
senses.titleCN: 灌丛中的野生动物生境
senses.definition: shrubland valued as cover and food for birds, reptiles and small mammals that avoid open ground
senses.definitionCN: 作为鸟类、爬行类与小型哺乳动物躲避开阔地的隐蔽与食物来源而受重视的灌丛
senses.example: Nesting hens need dense shrubland within reach of water.
senses.exampleCN: 筑巢的母鸡需要靠近水源的密灌丛。
senses.why: the cover type becomes a habitat term once managers ask which species need dense low woody growth.
senses.whyCN: 当管理者追问哪些物种需要低矮密灌时，覆盖类型就成了生境术语。

senses.title: Woody encroachment and degradation
senses.titleCN: 木本侵入与退化型灌丛
senses.definition: former grassland or pasture now thick with shrubs because grazing or fire regimes changed
senses.definitionCN: 因放牧或火烧制度改变而灌木丛生的原草地或牧场
senses.example: Encroaching shrubland has cut the pasture by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 侵入的灌丛已使牧场减少三分之一。
senses.why: the same cover can be a natural stage or a symptom, and the word carries whichever framing the user brings.
senses.whyCN: 同一种覆盖既可能是自然阶段，也可能是症状，用词随使用者的框架而定。

senses.title: A land-cover class on maps
senses.titleCN: 土地覆盖分类中的灌丛类
senses.definition: a mapped category for pixels or polygons whose dominant cover is woody plants below tree height
senses.definitionCN: 遥感或制图中，优势覆盖为低于乔木高度的木本植物的像元或多边形类别
senses.example: The classifier merges shrubland with young forest in this band.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一波段，分类器把灌丛与幼林并成一类。
senses.why: mapping needs mutually exclusive classes, so an ecological description is hardened into a label with thresholds.
senses.whyCN: 制图需要互斥类别，于是生态描述被固化为带阈值的标签。

intro.en: Shrubland is a transparent modern English compound of shrub and land, used mainly as an ecological and mapping term from the twentieth century.
intro.cn: shrubland 是 shrub 与 land 构成的现代英语透明复合词，主要自 20 世纪起作生态学与制图术语使用。

items.en: Shrub goes back to Old English scrybb 'brushwood, low woody growth', a North Sea Germanic word of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: shrub 上溯古英语 scrybb「柴枝、低矮木本植物」，是北海日耳曼词，更深来源不确定。

items.en: Land 'ground, territory' is native Germanic; the reconstructed *landam has no settled pre-Germanic source.
items.cn: land「土地、领土」是日耳曼本族词；重构形式 *landam 在日耳曼语之前没有定论来源。

items.en: Shrubland appears in English writing on vegetation in the nineteenth century, at first as plain description rather than a fixed class.
items.cn: shrubland 在 19 世纪的植被记述中出现，起初只是平实描述，并非固定类别。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology and land-cover mapping fixed shrubland as a cover class parallel to grassland and forest.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生态学与土地覆盖制图把 shrubland 固定为与草地、森林并列的覆盖类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest citation of the compound is not securely dated, and the pre-Germanic roots of both shrub and land are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：这个复合词的最早书证年代不可靠，shrub 与 land 的日耳曼语之前词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates the cover-type words that look alike; group two separates regional and structural near-synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形相近的覆盖类型词；第二组区分地区性与结构性近义词。

entries.definition: A planted shrub bed in a garden or park; it is a design feature, not a landscape cover type.
entries.definitionCN: 庭园或公园中栽植的灌木花坛；是设计元素，不是景观覆盖类型。

entries.definition: Land dominated by grasses rather than shrubs; the two classes compete where fire and grazing shift the balance.
entries.definitionCN: 以草而非灌木为主的土地；在火与放牧改变平衡之处，两类互相争夺。

entries.definition: Land with a tree canopy; shrubland lacks the canopy, even if both are low and dense.
entries.definitionCN: 有树冠的土地；灌丛没有树冠，尽管两者都可能低矮茂密。

entries.definition: An Australian term for shrub-and-tree country; it often includes scattered trees that shrubland excludes.
entries.definitionCN: 澳洲用语，指灌木与树相杂的地带；常含散生乔木，而灌丛不含。

entries.definition: Low, often stunted or thorny woody cover; close to shrubland but more negative and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 低矮、常矮小或多刺的木本覆盖；接近灌丛，但更负面、较少技术化。

entries.definition: Californian dense evergreen shrubland subject to crown fire; a regional name for one type.
entries.definitionCN: 加州受树冠火影响的常绿密灌丛；某一类型的地区名称。

entries.definition: Mediterranean scrub on siliceous soil, often tall and impenetrable; another regional name.
entries.definitionCN: 地中海硅质土上的灌丛，常高大难行；另一地区名称。

entries.definition: Open dwarf-shrub cover dominated by heather or heath plants on acid soil; narrower than shrubland.
entries.definitionCN: 酸性土上以石南类为主的矮灌丛；范围比 shrubland 窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: shrub + land: land whose crop is low woody plants.
normal.cn: shrub + land：以低矮木本植物为作物的土地。

normal.en: It sits between grassland and woodland in the cover ladder.
normal.cn: 在覆盖类型的阶梯上，它位于草地与林地之间。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: semi-arid shrubland, Mediterranean shrubland, shrubland habitat.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：半干旱灌丛、地中海灌丛、灌丛生境。

normal.en: Regional names for the same type: maquis, chaparral, garrigue.
normal.cn: 同一类型的地区名称：maquis、chaparral、garrigue。

normal.en: The image is a slope covered to the waist with shrubs and no high trees.
normal.cn: 意象是一片齐腰高、没有高树的坡地。

abstract.en: Think of a queue waiting for the forest's place, holding the ground meanwhile.
abstract.cn: 想象一支排队等森林位置的队伍，同时先替它守住地面。

abstract.en: Think of a low ceiling that blocks the light but not the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一层低矮的天花板，挡住光却挡不住风。

abstract.en: Think of a map legend that must choose one colour for a messy reality.
abstract.cn: 想象图例必须为混乱的现实只选一种颜色。

examples.en: Shrubland expanded after the sheep were removed.
examples.cn: 羊群撤走之后，灌丛扩大了。

examples.en: Fire is a natural part of this shrubland's cycle.
examples.cn: 火是这片灌丛循环中的自然一环。

examples.en: The survey maps shrubland separately from young plantation.
examples.cn: 这次调查把灌丛与幼林分开制图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「shrub（灌木）+ land（土地）」——长满灌木的土地 → 灌丛地

root: shrub（古英语 scrybb「柴枝、低矮木本植物」，北海日耳曼语，更深词源不确定）+ land（古英语 land「土地」，日耳曼语，*landam 为重构）。英语复合词，无拉丁成分。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat the same cover type as plant community, property, successional stage, climate zone, habitat, symptom and map class.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种覆盖类型分别当作植物群落、地块、演替阶段、气候带、生境、症状与地图类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a waist-high sea of shrubs with no tree canopy above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片齐腰高的灌木之海，上方没有树冠。

branches.en: COVER AND GROUND: the plants define the type, the land defines the unit.
branches.cn: 覆盖与地面：植物定义类型，土地定义单元。

branches.en: TIME: shrubland can be a passing stage or a lasting symptom of changed grazing and fire.
branches.cn: 时间：灌丛既可能是过渡阶段，也可能是放牧与火改变后的持久症状。

branches.en: CLIMATE: winter-wet or semi-arid, the type is fixed by rainfall and season.
branches.cn: 气候：无论冬雨还是半干旱，类型由降水与季节固定。

branches.en: HABITAT: dense low wood is cover and food for animals that avoid open ground.
branches.cn: 生境：低矮密林为躲避开阔地的动物提供隐蔽与食物。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION: ecology's description hardens into a map legend with thresholds.
branches.cn: 分类：生态描述固化为带阈值的图例。

intro.en: Shrubland is a two-word compound; its affix-like behaviour comes from the suffixes its first element can take.
intro.cn: shrubland 是两词复合；它类似词缀的行为来自第一个成分可接的后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is present: both halves are Germanic, so the Latin list stays empty rather than borrowing false relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 其中没有拉丁成分：两半都是日耳曼语，因此拉丁词条留空，不借假同族。

items.example: A shrub holds the dune crest.
items.exampleCN: 一株灌木固定住沙丘顶。

items.example: The land was never ploughed.
items.exampleCN: 这块地从未被犁过。

items.example: Shrubland replaced the burned forest.
items.exampleCN: 灌丛取代了烧毁的森林。

items.example: The shrubby flat is hard to cross.
items.exampleCN: 这片灌木平地很难穿行。

items.example: The shrubbery needs pruning.
items.exampleCN: 这片灌木区需要修剪。

items.example: A subshrub dies back to the base each winter.
items.exampleCN: 半灌木每年冬季枯到基部。

items.example: A shrub-dominated belt borders the salt flat.
items.exampleCN: 一条灌木占优的带子紧邻盐滩。

items.example: Shrub-steppe grades into true desert.
items.exampleCN: 灌木草原逐渐过渡为真正的荒漠。

definition_zh: 草地；草原；以草本植物为主的土地；牧场
definition_en: land covered mainly by grasses, with few or no trees
core_image: 一片望不到边的草地，草根在土里织成厚垫，地面上几乎看不到树
scene: 草根在土中织成厚厚一层垫子，使这片草原熬过几乎无雨的一年。Deep roots let this grassland survive a year of almost no rain.
sceneCN: 这里 grassland 指「以草本植物为主的土地」（第 1 个义项：草占优势、乔木稀少的植被覆盖）；句意为深长的草根让这片草原熬过几乎无雨的一年。图中可辨识物件：草穗、交错的根系、干裂表土、远处低平的地平线。

pos.zh: 草地；草原；牧场（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 草根；基层的（词义已转移）

senses.title: Land dominated by grass
senses.definition: a tract of ground whose main plant cover is grasses, with trees absent or too few to form a canopy
senses.definitionCN: 主要植物覆盖为草、乔木缺失或稀少到无法形成树冠的一片土地
senses.example: Deep roots let this grassland survive a year of almost no rain.
senses.exampleCN: 深长的草根让这片草原熬过几乎无雨的一年。
senses.why: grass plus land names ground by its dominant plant, exactly as woodland is named by trees.
senses.whyCN: grass 加 land 按优势植物给土地命名，正如 woodland 按树命名。

senses.title: Pasture and rangeland
senses.definition: grassland used for grazing livestock, whether sown or natural
senses.definitionCN: 用于放牧家畜的草地，无论人工播种还是天然
senses.example: The farm keeps two hundred ewes on the lower grassland.
senses.exampleCN: 农场在低处草地养着两百只母羊。
senses.why: once grass is harvested by animals rather than by machines, the word takes on the working sense of pasture.
senses.whyCN: 当草由牲畜而非机器收获，这个词就带上了「牧场」这一作业含义。

senses.title: The temperate grassland biome
senses.definition: the mid-latitude grass biome with hot summers, cold winters and too little rain for forest, as prairie, steppe or pampas
senses.definitionCN: 中纬度草地生物群系，夏热冬冷、降水不足以成林，如北美草原、干草原与潘帕斯
senses.example: Temperate grassland stores much of its carbon below ground.
senses.exampleCN: 温带草原把大部分碳储在地下。
senses.why: biogeography groups all such regions into one biome, so grassland becomes a global class rather than a local field.
senses.whyCN: 生物地理学把这类地区归为一个生物群系，于是 grassland 从本地田块变成全球类别。

senses.title: Tropical grassland with scattered trees
senses.definition: the tropical grass formation with a dry season and scattered drought-resistant trees, usually called savanna
senses.definitionCN: 有旱季、散生耐旱乔木的热带草地，通常称 savanna
senses.example: Tropical grassland turns brown within weeks of the last rain.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一场雨过后几周，热带草原就变成褐色。
senses.why: the same cover word serves the tropics, where grass is still dominant even when trees are present.
senses.whyCN: 同一个覆盖词也适用于热带：即使有树，草仍占优势。

senses.title: Grassland ecosystem services
senses.definition: the soil formation, water regulation and carbon storage that grass cover provides
senses.definitionCN: 草覆盖所提供的地壤形成、水分调节与碳储存
senses.example: Grassland holds water that bare fields would shed.
senses.exampleCN: 草地能蓄住裸地会流走的水。
senses.why: the dense root mat makes grassland a service provider, not merely a place where grass grows.
senses.whyCN: 密集根垫使草地成为服务提供者，而不只是长草的地方。

senses.title: Grassland restoration
senses.definition: the deliberate return of arable or degraded land to species-rich grass cover
senses.definitionCN: 有意把耕地或退化地恢复为物种丰富的草覆盖
senses.example: Sowing local seed is the first step in grassland restoration.
senses.exampleCN: 播下本地种子是草地恢复的第一步。
senses.why: conservation turned the cover word into a target: what was ploughed can be made grassland again.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作把这个覆盖词变成目标：被犁过的地可以重新变回草地。

senses.title: A land-cover class
senses.titleCN: 土地覆盖分类中的草地类
senses.definition: a mapped category for ground whose dominant cover is grass, distinct from crop and shrub classes
senses.definitionCN: 优势覆盖为草、与作物类和灌丛类相区别的制图类别
senses.example: The national map counts grassland and cropland separately.
senses.exampleCN: 全国地图把草地与耕地分开统计。
senses.why: mapping needs thresholds, so a loose botanical description becomes a labelled class with percentage rules.
senses.whyCN: 制图需要阈值，于是宽松的植物描述变成带百分比规则的标签类别。

senses.title: Managed turf and amenity grass
senses.titleCN: 人工管理的草坪与运动场草
senses.definition: grass kept short by mowing and irrigation for lawns, parks and sports pitches
senses.definitionCN: 通过修剪与灌溉保持低矮、用于草坪、公园与运动场的草
senses.example: The stadium grassland is mown three times a week.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场的草坪每周修剪三次。
senses.why: the same cover word extends to the most artificial grass of all, where management replaces climate.
senses.whyCN: 同一个覆盖词也延伸到最人工的草地：管理取代了气候。

intro.en: Grassland is a native English compound of grass and land; grass is Germanic and has a known Indo-European link to 'grow, green'.
intro.cn: grassland 是 grass 与 land 构成的英语本族复合词；grass 属日耳曼语，其印欧语联系「生长、绿色」较为可信。

items.en: Græs meant 'grass, herb'. It descends from Germanic *grasam, connected by the usual sound laws to the root that also gives grow and green.
items.cn: græs 意为「草、草本」。它来自日耳曼语 *grasam，按常规音变可联系到也产生 grow 与 green 的词根。

items.en: Land 'ground, territory' is Germanic *landam; its pre-Germanic origin is uncertain and any deeper form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: land「土地、领土」是日耳曼语 *landam；其在日耳曼语之前的来源不确定，更深形式均属重构。

items.en: The compound grassland is recorded in Middle English, naming ground grown to grass rather than the grass itself.
items.cn: 复合词 grassland 见于中古英语，指长草的地面，而非草本身。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century ecology fixed grassland as a biome and land-cover class beside forest and desert.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的生态学把 grassland 固定为与森林、荒漠并列的生物群系与覆盖类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation of grassland is not securely dated, and land's pre-Germanic root remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：grassland 的最早书证年代不可靠，land 的日耳曼语之前词根仍无定论。

note.en: Group one separates the parallel -land cover compounds; group two separates the working and regional words for grass cover.
note.cn: 第一组区分并列的 -land 覆盖复合词；第二组区分草地的作业词与地区词。

entries.definition: Land covered by trees; it is the cover class above grassland in the height ladder.
entries.definitionCN: 树木覆盖的土地；在高度阶梯上位于草地之上。

entries.definition: Land covered by low woody plants; it often replaces grassland when grazing or fire changes.
entries.definitionCN: 低矮木本植物覆盖的土地；放牧或火改变时，它常取代草地。

entries.definition: Land saturated or covered by water; the limiting factor is water, not plant form.
entries.definitionCN: 被水饱和或覆盖的土地；限制因子是水，而非植物形态。

entries.definition: Land sown to crops and harvested annually; it is a land-use class rather than a natural cover.
entries.definitionCN: 播种作物并每年收获的土地；是土地利用类别，而非自然覆盖。

entries.definition: Grassland managed for livestock; it stresses use, while grassland stresses cover.
entries.definitionCN: 为家畜经营的地；强调用途，而 grassland 强调覆盖。

entries.definition: Grassland kept for hay or left unmown for flowers, usually moist and small-scale.
entries.definitionCN: 用于制干草或任其开花不割的草地，通常湿润且面积较小。

entries.definition: The vast short-grass plain of Eurasia; a regional name for temperate grassland.
entries.definitionCN: 欧亚大陆广阔的短草平原；温带草原的地区名称。

entries.definition: Unenclosed land grazed extensively, including grass, shrub and open forest; broader than grassland.
entries.definitionCN: 广泛放牧的未围封土地，含草地、灌丛与疏林；比 grassland 宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: grass + land: land whose crop is grass.
normal.cn: grass + land：以草为作物的土地。

normal.en: The family runs grass, grassy, grassland, greensward.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 grass、grassy、grassland、greensward。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: temperate grassland, tropical grassland, native grassland, grassland restoration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：温带草原、热带草原、原生草地、草地恢复。

normal.en: The world's regional names: prairie, steppe, pampas, savanna.
normal.cn: 世界各地的地区名称：prairie、steppe、pampas、savanna。

normal.en: The image is a thick mat of roots holding soil under a flat sea of grass.
normal.cn: 意象是草海之下，一层厚根垫把土壤抓住。

abstract.en: Think of a carpet that repairs itself whenever it is cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一块被剪后能自行修补的地毯。

abstract.en: Think of a community that lives mostly underground and sends up thin green antennae.
abstract.cn: 想象一个多数成员住在地下、只伸出细绿触角的群落。

abstract.en: Think of a fire that clears the roof but leaves the floor intact.
abstract.cn: 想象一场火清掉了屋顶，却让地板完好。

examples.en: Ploughing up the grassland released carbon that had taken centuries to store.
examples.cn: 犁开草地释放了储存数百年之久的碳。

examples.en: The grassland bird needs grass tall enough to hide its nest.
examples.cn: 草原鸟类需要足够高的草来藏巢。

examples.en: Grazing at the right season keeps the grassland from scrubbing over.
examples.cn: 在合适季节放牧，可以防止草地被灌丛侵占。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「grass（草）+ land（土地）」——长草的土地 → 草地、草原

root: grass（古英语 græs「草」，日耳曼语 *grasam，与 grow/green 同根）+ land（古英语 land「土地」，日耳曼语 *landam）。英语复合词，无拉丁成分；land 的更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from simple grass cover to grazing land, global biome, ecosystem service, restoration target and finally mown turf.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从简单的草覆盖，走向放牧地、全球生物群系、生态服务、恢复目标，最后到修剪的草坪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat sea of grass over a dense mat of roots.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片平展的草海，下面是一层密集的根垫。

branches.en: COVER: grass dominance defines the ground, whether seen in the field or on a map.
branches.cn: 覆盖：草占优势定义这块地，无论在地头还是在图上。

branches.en: USE: animals harvest the grass, and the cover becomes pasture.
branches.cn: 用途：牲畜收获草，覆盖便成为牧场。

branches.en: CLIMATE: the same formation appears as temperate prairie or tropical savanna.
branches.cn: 气候：同一群系表现为温带草原或热带草原。

branches.en: VALUE: roots build soil and hold water, and lost grass can be restored.
branches.cn: 价值：根建造土壤、蓄住水，失去的草可以恢复。

branches.en: ARTIFICE: mowing and irrigation push the cover to its most managed form.
branches.cn: 人工：修剪与灌溉把覆盖推到最受管理的形态。

intro.en: Grassland is a native two-word compound; its family is built by suffixes added to grass rather than by prefixes.
intro.cn: grassland 是本族两词复合；其词族主要靠在 grass 上加后缀构成，而非加前缀。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: grass and land are Germanic, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁语：grass 与 land 属日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: The grass was grazed down to the root.
items.exampleCN: 草被啃到根部。

items.example: The land lies low and wet.
items.exampleCN: 这块地低洼潮湿。

items.example: The grassland runs to the horizon.
items.exampleCN: 草地一直延伸到地平线。

items.example: A grassy bank borders the stream.
items.exampleCN: 一道长草的岸贴着溪流。

items.example: The grassed bund held the water.
items.exampleCN: 播过草的土埂拦住了水。

items.example: Overgrazing left a grassless slope.
items.exampleCN: 过牧留下了一片无草的坡。

items.meaning: the ordinary level of an organization
items.meaningCN: 基层；草根层（词义已转移）
items.example: The movement began at the grassroot level.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动从基层开始。

items.example: Grass-fed cattle need wide grassland.
items.exampleCN: 草饲牛需要宽阔的草地。

definition_zh: （北美）草原；大草原；高草草原；草原带
definition_en: the extensive temperate grassland of North America, especially the treeless plain of the interior
core_image: 春天火烧过后，黑色残茬之上抽出新绿，平原一直铺到天边，中间没有一棵树
scene: 春季火烧之后，嫩芽从黑色残茬里钻出，一直铺到地平线。After the spring burn, new shoots rise through the black stubble across the prairie.
sceneCN: 这里 prairie 指「北美内陆广阔的无树草原」（第 1 个义项：北美温带大草原）；句意为春季火烧之后，新芽从黑色残茬中钻出，铺满整片草原。图中可辨识物件：黑色残茬、嫩绿新芽、低平天际线、远处无树。

pos.zh: 北美草原；大草原（可数或不可数）
草原的（多作定语）

collocations.zh: 草原壶穴（冰蚀洼地湿地）

derivatives.zh: 草原大篷车（拓荒者马车）

senses.title: The North American treeless plain
senses.definition: the vast interior grassland of North America, largely treeless and once covered in perennial grasses
senses.definitionCN: 北美内陆广阔草地，基本无树，曾覆盖多年生草类
senses.example: After the spring burn, new shoots rise through the black stubble across the prairie.
senses.exampleCN: 春季火烧之后，嫩芽从黑色残茬中钻出，铺满整片草原。
senses.why: English borrowed the French word for meadow and applied it to a grassland on a scale French meadows never had.
senses.whyCN: 英语借来法语「草地」一词，却用在一个远比法国草地辽阔的草原上。

senses.title: Tallgrass prairie
senses.definition: the moist eastern prairie where grasses grow taller than a person, rooted in deep dark soil
senses.definitionCN: 较湿润的东部草原，草高过人，扎根于深厚黑土
senses.example: Big bluestem can reach two metres in a tallgrass prairie.
senses.exampleCN: 在高草草原上，大须芒草能长到两米。
senses.why: rainfall along the eastern margin lets the same biome grow tall, so the type is named by the grass height.
senses.whyCN: 东缘降水较多，让同一生物群系长出高草，于是按草高命名类型。

senses.title: Shortgrass prairie
senses.definition: the dry western prairie where grazing and low rainfall keep grasses short and the ground partly bare
senses.definitionCN: 干旱的西部草原，放牧与低降水使草保持低矮，地面部分裸露
senses.example: Shortgrass prairie survives on less than forty centimetres of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 短草草原靠不足四十厘米的降水存活。
senses.why: the same formation thins westward, and the height of the grass becomes the diagnostic feature.
senses.whyCN: 同一群系向西变稀，草的高度成了鉴别特征。

senses.title: Mixed-grass prairie
senses.definition: the transitional prairie between tall and short types, where both height classes grow together
senses.definitionCN: 介于高草与短草类型之间的过渡草原，两个高度级混生
senses.example: Mixed-grass prairie shifts its balance with each wet or dry decade.
senses.exampleCN: 混草草原的平衡随每个湿润或干旱的十年而移动。
senses.why: where rainfall is intermediate, neither height class wins, so the type is named for the mixture itself.
senses.whyCN: 降水居中之处，两个高度级都不占绝对优势，于是类型按混合本身命名。

senses.title: Prairie soil and the farm belt
senses.definition: the deep, dark, nutrient-rich soil formed under prairie grass, and the farmland that uses it
senses.definitionCN: 草原草类下形成的深厚、暗色、富养分的土壤，以及利用它的农田
senses.example: Prairie soil still yields some of the world's highest maize crops.
senses.exampleCN: 草原土至今仍产出世界上最高的玉米产量之一。
senses.why: centuries of grass roots built the soil, so the land's name transferred to the soil and then to the crops grown on it.
senses.whyCN: 数百年的草根造出这种土，于是地名先转到土壤，再转到其上种的作物。

senses.title: Prairie restoration and reconstruction
senses.definition: the replanting of native prairie species on former farmland to rebuild the grassland community
senses.definitionCN: 在退耕地上补种原生草原物种，以重建草原群落
senses.example: Volunteers hand-collect seed for prairie restoration each August.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者每年八月手工采集种子，用于草原恢复。
senses.why: restoration distinguishes a reconstructed prairie from a remnant one, a difference the word alone does not show.
senses.whyCN: 恢复工作把重建草原与残存草原区分开，而单词本身并不显示这一区别。

senses.title: Prairie pothole wetlands
senses.definition: the shallow ice-formed depressions that hold water within the prairie and support breeding ducks
senses.definitionCN: 草原上由冰蚀形成、积水的浅洼地，供养繁殖的鸭类
senses.example: Each prairie pothole can raise dozens of ducklings a year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个草原壶穴每年能养大几十只小鸭。
senses.why: the prairie is not uniform: small wetlands embedded in it carry a name built from the grassland word.
senses.whyCN: 草原并不均质：嵌入其中的小湿地也带着草原之名的构造。

senses.title: The Canadian Prairies as a region
senses.definition: the wheat-growing provinces of Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta, named after their grassland cover
senses.definitionCN: 以草原覆盖得名的曼尼托巴、萨斯喀彻温与艾伯塔三省农业区
senses.example: Grain from the Prairies moves by rail to the lake ports.
senses.exampleCN: 草原三省的谷物经铁路运往湖港。
senses.why: a cover word became a proper regional name, so capitalised Prairies now means a political and economic unit.
senses.whyCN: 覆盖词变成了专有地区名，因此大写的「草原三省」现在指一个政治与经济单元。

intro.en: Prairie is a French loan: Old French praerie and Medieval Latin prataria both go back to Latin pratum 'meadow', so the word has a clear Latin line.
intro.cn: prairie 是法语借词：古法语 praerie 与中世纪拉丁 prataria 都上溯拉丁 pratum「草地」，因此有清楚的拉丁线索。

items.en: Pratum meant 'meadow'. Its further origin is debated; a link to a root meaning 'bent, spread out' is offered as a hypothesis, not a proof.
items.cn: pratum 意为「草地」。其更早来源有争论，有人提出与表示「弯曲、铺展」的词根相关，但那只是假说，并非证明。

items.en: Prataria 'meadow land' extended pratum to the ground rather than the crop of grass.
items.cn: prataria「草地」把 pratum 从草产扩展到土地本身。

items.en: Old French praerie passed into English in the seventeenth century as prairie, at first simply 'meadow'.
items.cn: 古法语 praerie 在 17 世纪以 prairie 进入英语，最初只是「草地」。

items.en: Explorers applied the familiar French word to the immense treeless grasslands of the interior, and the American sense displaced the older one.
items.cn: 探险者把这个熟悉的法语词用在内陆广袤无树的草原上，美洲义逐渐取代旧义。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of pratum is unsettled, and the exact date when prairie narrowed to the North American plain is not securely attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定：pratum 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论；prairie 收窄为北美平原的确切年代亦无可靠书证。

note.en: Group one collects the regional names for grasslands that are easily swapped; group two collects the general and local grass-cover words.
note.cn: 第一组是易被互换的各地草原名称；第二组是通用的与局部的草覆盖词。

entries.definition: The short-grass plain of Eurasia, from Ukrainian step; similar in form to prairie but a different continent and climate.
entries.definitionCN: 欧亚短草平原，来自乌克兰语 step；形态与 prairie 相近，但属不同大陆与气候。

entries.definition: The fertile grass plains of Argentina and Uruguay, from Quechua pampa 'plain'; often used in the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 阿根廷与乌拉圭的肥沃草原，来自克丘亚语 pampa「平原」；常用复数。

entries.definition: Tropical grassland with scattered trees; it has a dry season and a tree layer that prairie lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 带散生树的热带草原；有旱季与 prairie 所无的乔木层。

entries.definition: Open grassland of southern Africa, from Afrikaans veld 'field'; it ranges from sweet to sour grass types.
entries.definitionCN: 南部非洲开阔草地，来自南非荷兰语 veld「田野」；分甜草与酸草类型。

entries.definition: Any land dominated by grass; prairie is the North American member of this class.
entries.definitionCN: 任何以草为主的土地；prairie 是该类中的北美成员。

entries.definition: A small grass field kept for hay or flowers; the scale is a field, not a subcontinent.
entries.definitionCN: 用于干草或观花的小片草地；尺度是一块田，而非次大陆。

entries.definition: A flat expanse of land, which may be grass, desert or even ice; it names shape, not cover.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦的大片土地，可能是草地、荒漠甚至冰面；命名的是地形，不是覆盖。

entries.definition: Open land used for grazing, in North America often shortened from rangeland; it stresses use.
entries.definitionCN: 用于放牧的开阔地，在北美常为 rangeland 的简称；强调用途。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: prairie is French for meadow, applied to a whole continent's grass.
normal.cn: prairie 本是法语「草地」，却被用在一整块大陆的草上。

normal.en: The Latin line: pratum 'meadow' → prataria → praerie → prairie.
normal.cn: 拉丁线索：pratum「草地」→ prataria → praerie → prairie。

normal.en: Height names the types: tallgrass, mixed-grass, shortgrass.
normal.cn: 高度命名类型：高草、混草、短草。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: prairie soil, prairie fire, prairie pothole, prairie dog.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：草原土、草原火、草原壶穴、草原犬鼠。

normal.en: Capitalised Prairies names the Canadian wheat provinces.
normal.cn: 大写的 Prairies 指加拿大草原三省。

abstract.en: Think of a lawn the size of a sea, mown by fire instead of a machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海那么大的草坪，由火而非机器来修剪。

abstract.en: Think of soil built upward over centuries by roots that never stop reaching down.
abstract.cn: 想象土壤被从不停止向下伸的根，用几百年时间向上造出。

abstract.en: Think of a name for a meadow that grew until the meadow became a country.
abstract.cn: 想象一个「草地」之名不断长大，直到草地变成一个地区。

examples.en: Less than one per cent of the original tallgrass prairie remains.
examples.cn: 原有高草草原留存不足百分之一。

examples.en: The prairie wind carries seed for kilometres.
examples.cn: 草原风能把种子带出数公里。

examples.en: They planted prairie strips between the maize fields to hold soil.
examples.cn: 他们在玉米田之间种下草原草带以保住土壤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「prairie」听起来像「 prairie 铺到天边」——法语「草地」被用来称北美大草原

root: 拉丁 pratum「草地」→ 中世纪拉丁 prataria「草地」→ 古法语 praerie → 英语 prairie。pratum 的拉丁语之前来源有争议，相关词根联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide the North American grassland by grass height, soil, restoration, embedded wetlands and finally by the Canadian region it named.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按草高、土壤、恢复、嵌入式湿地，最后按它所命名的加拿大地区，把北美草原分切开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unbroken grass plain reaching the horizon with no tree in sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片不断的草平原直到天边，望不见一棵树。

branches.en: BASE: the borrowed word fixes on a treeless plain of continental scale.
branches.cn: 基底：这个借词固定在大陆尺度的无树平原上。

branches.en: RAINFALL: wet east grows tall grass, dry west short grass, and the middle mixes both.
branches.cn: 降水：湿润的东部长大草，干旱的西部长短草，中间两者混合。

branches.en: SOIL: grass roots become deep dark earth, and the earth becomes a farm belt.
branches.cn: 土壤：草根变成深厚黑土，黑土又变成农业带。

branches.en: FRAGMENTS: what remains is restored by hand or survives as potholes inside farmland.
branches.cn: 残片：所剩者或靠人工恢复，或作为农田中的壶穴存留。

branches.en: NAME: the cover word hardens into the proper name of three provinces.
branches.cn: 名称：覆盖词固化为三个省的专名。

intro.en: Prairie is a borrowed simplex, not a prefixed word; its family grows through compounds such as prairie dog and prairie fire.
intro.cn: prairie 是借来的单纯词，不带前缀；其词族靠 prairie dog、prairie fire 这类复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin pratum and Medieval Latin prataria are the documented ancestors; the French form praerie is the immediate source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pratum 与中世纪拉丁 prataria 是有文献的祖先；法语形式 praerie 是直接来源。

items.example: The prairie lay flat to the west.
items.exampleCN: 草原向西平铺而去。

items.example: Latin pratum names a mown grass field.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 pratum 指可割草的田。

items.example: Prataria widened the crop word to the ground.
items.exampleCN: prataria 把这个作物词扩到土地。

items.meaningCN: 一种穴居草原啮齿动物
items.example: A prairie dog town can hold thousands of burrows.
items.exampleCN: 一个草原犬鼠聚落可有上千个洞穴。

items.example: A prairie fire moves faster than a person can run.
items.exampleCN: 草原火的速度快过人跑。

items.meaning: dark fertile soil formed under grass
items.meaningCN: 草下形成的暗色肥沃土壤
items.example: Prairie soil is deep and high in humus.
items.exampleCN: 草原土深厚且腐殖质高。

items.example: Ducks nest around every prairie pothole.
items.exampleCN: 鸭子在每个草原壶穴周围筑巢。

items.example: Tallgrass prairie needs periodic fire.
items.exampleCN: 高草草原需要周期性火烧。

definition_zh: 热带草原；（带散生乔木的）稀树草原；萨瓦纳
definition_en: tropical or subtropical grassland with scattered trees and a marked dry season
core_image: 旱季末尾，金黄的草海上零星立着几棵伞形金合欢，树影很短
scene: 旱季将尽，草海变成金黄色，零星的金合欢撑着伞形树冠立在其间。In this savanna scattered acacias stand above a sea of grass that turns gold by the end of the dry season.
sceneCN: 这里 savanna 指「有旱季、散生乔木的热带草原」（第 1 个义项：稀树草原）；句意为在这片稀树草原上，零星金合欢立在旱季末尾变金的草海之上。图中可辨识物件：伞形树冠、金黄草层、短树影、远处灰白天空。

pos.zh: 稀树草原；热带草原（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 稀树草原化（森林退为稀树草原）

senses.title: Tropical grass with scattered trees
senses.definition: a tropical formation in which a continuous grass layer carries scattered trees, with a pronounced dry season
senses.definitionCN: 连续的草层上散布乔木、并有明显旱季的热带植被类型
senses.example: In this savanna scattered acacias stand above a sea of grass that turns gold by the end of the dry season.
senses.exampleCN: 在这片稀树草原上，零星金合欢立在旱季末尾变金的草海之上。
senses.why: the word names a mixture, not a pure type: grass is continuous, trees are present but never close a canopy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一种混合，而非纯型：草层连续，树虽有却从不闭合树冠。

senses.title: A climate with a long dry season
senses.titleCN: 有明显旱季的草原气候
senses.definition: the tropical climate type with a wet season and a long dry season, classified Aw in Koppen's scheme
senses.definitionCN: 有雨季与长旱季的热带气候型，在柯本分类中属热带干湿季气候
senses.example: The savanna climate gives eight dry months and four wet ones.
senses.exampleCN: 稀树草原气候给出八个月旱季与四个月雨季。
senses.why: the vegetation type gave its name to the climate that produces it, since the dry season is what keeps trees apart.
senses.whyCN: 植被类型为造成它的气候命名，因为正是旱季让树彼此分开。

senses.title: Savanna woodland structure
senses.definition: a savanna in which trees are dense enough to form a broken canopy over the grass
senses.definitionCN: 树木密到能在草层上方形成断续树冠的稀树草原
senses.example: Savanna woodland shades out the tallest grasses beneath it.
senses.exampleCN: 稀树草原林地把下方最高的草遮死。
senses.why: adding woodland marks the upper end of tree density, where the mixture begins to look like open forest.
senses.whyCN: 加上「疏林」标出树木密度的上端，此时混合已开始像疏林。

senses.title: Habitat for large grazers
senses.definition: the grass-and-tree mosaic that supports herds, their predators and seasonal migration
senses.definitionCN: 支撑兽群、捕食者与季节性迁徙的草树镶嵌体
senses.example: The savanna feeds the largest land migration on Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 这片稀树草原供养着地球上规模最大的陆地迁徙。
senses.why: the mixture offers grass for grazers and cover for hunters, so the type becomes shorthand for a whole fauna.
senses.whyCN: 混合结构为食草者提供草、为猎手提供隐蔽，于是这一类型成了一整套动物群的代称。

senses.title: A fire-maintained landscape
senses.definition: a savanna whose open structure persists only because repeated fires kill young trees
senses.definitionCN: 只有反复火烧杀死幼树，其开阔结构才得以维持的稀树草原
senses.example: Without savanna fire, the grass would close into thicket.
senses.exampleCN: 没有稀树草原火，草地将闭合成灌丛。
senses.why: fire is not a disturbance here but a maintenance tool, which is why the type is described as fire-dependent.
senses.whyCN: 在此火不是干扰而是维护手段，因此该类型被称为依赖火。

senses.title: Derived savanna from cleared forest
senses.titleCN: 由森林清除形成的次生稀树草原
senses.definition: grass-and-tree land produced by clearing or repeated burning of former forest
senses.definitionCN: 由清除或反复焚烧原森林而形成的草树混合地
senses.example: Much of the derived savanna was forest two generations ago.
senses.exampleCN: 大片次生稀树草原在两代人以前还是森林。
senses.why: the same cover can be ancient or recent, and 'derived' marks the human-made version.
senses.whyCN: 同样的覆盖既可能是古老的，也可能是新近的，「派生」一词标出人为形成的那一种。

senses.title: The ancient spread of C4 grassland
senses.titleCN: 古生态中四碳草地的扩张
senses.definition: the Miocene expansion of tropical grass biomes as C4 grasses and seasonal rainfall spread
senses.definitionCN: 随四碳草类与季节性降水扩张而发生的中新世热带草地扩展
senses.example: The savanna expanded as C4 grasses spread across the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 随着四碳草类在热带扩散，稀树草原也扩张。
senses.why: palaeoecology uses the modern cover word for a deep-time event, because the same structure can be read from fossils.
senses.whyCN: 古生态学用现代覆盖词指深时事件，因为同样的结构可从化石中读出。

senses.title: The savannah spelling variant
senses.definition: an alternative spelling with a doubled n, common in place names and in older British writing
senses.definitionCN: 双写 n 的异体拼写，常见于地名与较早的英式书写
senses.example: Older maps print savannah where modern surveys write savanna.
senses.exampleCN: 旧地图印作 savannah，现代调查写作 savanna。
senses.why: the doubled form reflects an earlier attempt to render the Spanish source; both spellings name the same cover.
senses.whyCN: 双写形式反映早期对西班牙语来源的转写尝试；两种拼写都指同一种覆盖。

intro.en: Savanna is a New World loan, probably from a Carib or Taino word for open grass, carried into English through Spanish sabana.
intro.cn: savanna 是新大陆借词，很可能出自加勒比或泰诺语表示开阔草地的词，经西班牙语 sabana 进入英语。

items.en: The source is usually given as a Carib or Taino word meaning 'open grassland' or 'plain'. The exact form and language are not settled.
items.cn: 来源通常被说成加勒比语或泰诺语中表示「开阔草地、平原」的词。确切形式与语种并无定论。

items.en: Spanish sabana recorded the word in the sixteenth century and passed it to other European languages.
items.cn: 西班牙语 sabana 在 16 世纪记录了这个词，并把它传给其他欧洲语言。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, first describing Caribbean and South American plains.
items.cn: 英语在 16 至 17 世纪借入，最初描述加勒比与南美的平原。

items.en: Colonial writers later applied the American word to African grass-and-tree country, and that usage now dominates.
items.cn: 殖民时期的作者后来把这个美洲词用在非洲的草树地带，这一用法如今占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (language and first date): the Carib/Taino origin is a common attribution rather than a documented derivation, and the first English citation is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（语种与首见年代）：加勒比/泰诺来源属常见归属，并非有文献证明的派生；最早英语书证年代亦不可靠。

note.en: Group one gathers the regional grass-and-tree names often used interchangeably; group two gathers the general cover words around them.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换的各地草树地带名称；第二组是周边通用的覆盖词。

entries.definition: The doubled-n spelling of the same word, frequent in place names such as Savannah, Georgia.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的双写 n 拼法，常见于地名，如佐治亚州的萨凡纳。

entries.definition: North American temperate grassland with essentially no trees, unlike savanna.
entries.definitionCN: 北美温带草原，基本无树，与稀树草原不同。

entries.definition: Eurasian short-grass plain with cold winters; it lacks the tropical dry season of savanna.
entries.definitionCN: 冬季寒冷的欧亚短草平原；没有稀树草原的热带旱季。

entries.definition: Southern African open grassland; some types approach savanna but the term is regional.
entries.definitionCN: 南部非洲开阔草地；某些类型接近稀树草原，但该词是地区性的。

entries.definition: Any grass-dominated land; savanna is the tropical, tree-dotted member of the class.
entries.definitionCN: 任何以草为主的土地；savanna 是该类中热带、带散生树的成员。

entries.definition: Southern African savanna with abundant shrubs; it stresses the woody component.
entries.definitionCN: 灌木丰富的南部非洲稀树草原；强调木本成分。

entries.definition: The seasonally flooded plains of the Orinoco basin; a regional savanna type.
entries.definitionCN: 奥里诺科河流域季节性泛滥的平原；一种地区性稀树草原。

entries.definition: Brazilian tropical savanna with twisted trees and deep roots; a regional type with its own flora.
entries.definitionCN: 巴西热带稀树草原，树形扭曲、根深；有独特植物区系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Grass continuous, trees scattered, dry season long: that is the savanna formula.
normal.cn: 草层连续、树木散布、旱季漫长：这就是稀树草原的公式。

normal.en: The route is Carib/Taino → Spanish sabana → English savanna.
normal.cn: 路径是加勒比/泰诺语 → 西班牙语 sabana → 英语 savanna。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: savanna climate, savanna woodland, savanna fire.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：稀树草原气候、稀树草原林地、草原火。

normal.en: Regional cousins: llanos, cerrado, bushveld, veld.
normal.cn: 地区近亲：llanos、cerrado、bushveld、veld。

normal.en: The image is a gold grass sea with a few umbrella acacias.
normal.cn: 意象是金黄草海上立着几棵伞形金合欢。

abstract.en: Think of a lawn that keeps a few trees on purpose so animals have both food and shade.
abstract.cn: 想象一片故意留下几棵树的草地，让动物既有食物又有荫。

abstract.en: Think of a balance held in place by fire, not by climate alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一种平衡靠火而非仅靠气候维持。

abstract.en: Think of a word borrowed from one continent and then rented out to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从一块大陆借来、又转租给另一块大陆的词。

examples.en: Elephants push over savanna trees to reach the grass below.
examples.cn: 大象推倒稀树草原上的树，以吃到下面的草。

examples.en: Savanna fires recycle nutrients faster than decomposition can.
examples.cn: 稀树草原火循环养分的速度快于分解。

examples.en: The boundary between forest and savanna shifts with rainfall.
examples.cn: 森林与稀树草原的边界随降水移动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「savanna」谐音「沙凡纳」——沙地上稀疏长着伞形树的草原 → 稀树草原

root: 可能出自加勒比语或泰诺语表示「开阔草地」的词 → 西班牙语 sabana → 英语 savanna。确切语种与形式不确定，属常见归属而非有文献证明的派生。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses read the same mixture as vegetation, climate, woodland, habitat, fire regime, derived land, fossil record and spelling variant.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种混合分别读成植被、气候、林地、生境、火情制度、次生地、化石记录与拼写变体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gold sea of grass with a few umbrella-shaped trees above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：金黄的草海之上立着几棵伞形树。

branches.en: MIXTURE: continuous grass and scattered trees, produced by a long dry season.
branches.cn: 混合：连续草层与散生树，由漫长旱季造成。

branches.en: DENSITY: as trees thicken, the same cover approaches woodland.
branches.cn: 密度：树变密时，同一覆盖接近疏林。

branches.en: FAUNA AND FIRE: grass feeds herds, cover hides hunters, and fire keeps the trees young.
branches.cn: 动物与火：草养兽群，树提供隐蔽，火让树保持幼态。

branches.en: TIME: the cover can be made by clearing or read back into the Miocene fossil record.
branches.cn: 时间：这种覆盖可由清林造成，也可回读至中新世化石记录。

branches.en: SPELLING: a doubled n marks the older transcription, not a different landscape.
branches.cn: 拼写：双写 n 只标出较早的转写，并非另一种景观。

intro.en: Savanna is a borrowed simplex with no productive affixes of its own; its family is made of compounds and regional names.
intro.cn: savanna 是借来的单纯词，本身不带能产后缀；其词族由复合词与地区名构成。

latinIntro.en: The immediate source is Spanish, but the word's deeper origin is American, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是西班牙语，但更深来源属美洲语言，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The savanna stretched to the river.
items.exampleCN: 稀树草原一直伸到河边。

items.example: Old charts write savannah.
items.exampleCN: 旧海图写作 savannah。

items.meaning: savanna with a broken tree canopy
items.meaningCN: 有断续树冠的稀树草原
items.example: Savanna woodland borders the river.
items.exampleCN: 稀树草原林地沿河分布。

items.example: The savanna climate suits drought-hardy crops.
items.exampleCN: 稀树草原气候适合耐旱作物。

items.example: Savanna fire clears young saplings.
items.exampleCN: 草原火清除幼树。

items.example: Savannization followed repeated burning.
items.exampleCN: 反复焚烧之后出现稀树草原化。

items.meaning: the grass-tree system as a whole
items.example: The savanna ecosystem depends on seasonal rain.
items.exampleCN: 稀树草原生态系统依赖季节性降水。

items.example: Dry savanna grades into thorn scrub.
items.exampleCN: 干旱稀树草原逐渐过渡为刺灌丛。

definition_zh: 沙漠；荒漠；荒凉之地；抛弃；擅离（职守）；（地方）空无一人的（名词与动词读音不同）
definition_en: a region so dry that it supports only sparse vegetation; also to abandon a person, place or duty
core_image: 沙与石一直铺到天边，中间没有水，也没有连续的草；风把沙脊推成一道一道
scene: 沙与石一直铺到天边，没有水，也没有连续的草。Nothing but sand and stone lay between us and the horizon in that desert.
sceneCN: 这里 desert 指「降水极少、植被稀疏的荒漠地区」（第 1 个义项：干旱荒漠）；句意为在那片荒漠里，我们与地平线之间只有沙与石。图中可辨识物件：沙脊、砾石、无草的砾漠面、远处平直地平线。

pos.zh: 沙漠；荒漠；荒凉之地（重音在前）
抛弃；遗弃；擅离（职守）（重音在后）
荒凉的；无人居住的（常以过去分词形式作定语）

senses.title: A region of extreme dryness
senses.definition: a region where evaporation greatly exceeds rainfall, so that continuous plant cover cannot form
senses.definitionCN: 蒸发远大于降水的地区，因而无法形成连续植被覆盖
senses.example: Nothing but sand and stone lay between us and the horizon in that desert.
senses.exampleCN: 在那片荒漠里，我们与地平线之间只有沙与石。
senses.why: the noun began as 'abandoned land', and the physical dryness sense grew from land nobody could use.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词原指「被弃置的土地」，物理上的干旱义正是从无人能用的土地生长出来。

senses.title: A sand sea or erg
senses.definition: the sandy subtype of desert, where wind builds dunes over a large area
senses.definitionCN: 荒漠的沙质亚型，风在大面积上堆出沙丘
senses.example: The erg is only one kind of desert, and it covers a small share of the Sahara.
senses.exampleCN: 沙海只是荒漠的一种，在撒哈拉中占比很小。
senses.why: popular images reduce desert to sand, but geographers separate the sandy erg from stony and gravel plains.
senses.whyCN: 大众印象把荒漠缩成沙，但地理学者把沙质沙丘地与石质、砾质平原分开。

senses.title: A cold desert
senses.definition: a dry region kept barren by cold or by rain shadow rather than by heat, as in polar or high-plateau deserts
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷或雨影而非高温而贫瘠的干旱地区，如极地或高原荒漠
senses.example: The Antarctic is the largest desert on Earth by rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 按降水量算，南极洲是地球上最大的荒漠。
senses.why: the defining variable is moisture deficit, not temperature, so ice and cold rock qualify.
senses.whyCN: 决定变量是水分亏缺而非温度，因此冰盖与冷岩也算。

senses.title: A barren or empty place
senses.titleCN: 荒凉或空无的地方（比喻）
senses.definition: a place or field felt to be without life, interest or supply, as in a cultural desert
senses.definitionCN: 让人觉得没有生机、趣味或供给的地方或领域，如「文化荒漠」
senses.example: The town was a cultural desert after the theatre closed.
senses.exampleCN: 剧院关闭后，这座小镇成了文化荒漠。
