senses.why: the metaphor keeps the old sense of abandonment: what is called a desert has been left empty of what matters.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留「被弃置」的旧义：被称作荒漠者，是被抽空了重要东西的地方。

senses.title: Abandon a person
senses.definition: to leave a person without help or support, especially someone to whom one owes loyalty
senses.definitionCN: 抛下某人使其失去帮助或支持，尤指对之有忠诚义务者
senses.example: He deserted his family when the debts came due.
senses.exampleCN: 债务到期时他抛弃了家人。
senses.why: the verb is the original idea behind the noun: deserere meant 'to undo a bond', and the wasteland was land whose bonds were undone.
senses.whyCN: 动词才是名词背后的原初观念：deserere 意为「解开联结」，荒漠就是联结被解开的地。

senses.title: Abandon a post or duty
senses.definition: to leave military or civil duty without permission, a punishable offence
senses.definitionCN: 未经许可离开军事或公职岗位，属可罚之罪
senses.example: A soldier who deserts in wartime faces a court martial.
senses.exampleCN: 战时擅离的士兵要受军事法庭审判。
senses.why: military law sharpened the general sense into a specific offence with its own noun, desertion.
senses.whyCN: 军事法把一般义收紧为有专名的「擅离职守罪」。

senses.title: Leave a place empty
senses.definition: to empty a place of its people, so that streets and buildings stand unused
senses.definitionCN: 使某地的人离去，街道与建筑因此空置
senses.example: The mills closed and the valley gradually deserted.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后，山谷渐渐空无一人。
senses.why: the participle deserted turned the act into a visible state, which is why it now works as an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词形式把动作变成可见状态，因此现在可作形容词。

senses.title: Forsake a cause or allegiance
senses.titleCN: 背弃某事业或效忠对象
senses.definition: to withdraw support from a party, cause or belief one formerly backed
senses.definitionCN: 撤回对原先支持的党派、事业或信念的支持
senses.example: Several donors deserted the campaign after the scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻之后，几位捐助者背弃了这场运动。
senses.why: the abstract sense extends abandonment from persons and posts to loyalties, where nothing physical is left behind.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把抛弃从人与岗位扩展到忠诚，此时并没有留下任何实体。

intro.en: Both the noun and the verb go back to Latin deserere 'to abandon', so the wasteland and the act of forsaking are one word at the root.
intro.cn: 名词与动词都上溯拉丁 deserere「抛弃」，因此「荒漠」与「背弃」在词根上本是同一个词。

items.en: Serere meant 'to join, weave, bind together'. Its participle sertus underlies a series of English words about linking and arranging.
items.cn: serere 意为「连接、编织、捆在一起」。其分词 sertus 构成一组关于连接与排列的英语词。

items.en: De- 'un-' plus serere produced deserere 'to undo the bond, abandon'. The image is not walking away but breaking a tie.
items.cn: de-「解除」加 serere 构成 deserere「解开联结、抛弃」。其意象不是走开，而是扯断一条纽带。

items.en: The neuter participle desertum meant 'an abandoned place', hence waste ground; English took it through Old French desert.
items.cn: 中性分词 desertum 意为「被弃置之处」，因而指荒地；英语经古法语 desert 借入。

items.en: English keeps both readings: the noun for the dry waste, the verb for the act of forsaking, distinguished today mainly by pronunciation.
items.cn: 英语保留两条读法：名词指干旱荒地，动词指抛弃行为，如今主要靠读音区分。

items.en: Just deserts 'what one deserves' is not this word at all: it comes from deserve, from Latin deservire 'to serve well'. The single r versus double r is decisive.
items.cn: just deserts「应得的报应」根本不是这个词：它来自 deserve，出自拉丁 deservire「尽力服务」。单 r 与双 r 是关键区别。

note.en: Group one separates the spelling traps that surround desert; group two separates the landscape words it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组拆开 desert 周围的拼写陷阱；第二组区分易与之混淆的地貌词。

entries.definition: The sweet course at the end of a meal, from French desservir 'to clear the table'; it is unrelated to desert.
entries.definitionCN: 餐末甜点，来自法语 desservir「撤去餐具」；与 desert 无关。

entries.definition: The participle and adjective from the verb desert, meaning emptied of people, not 'like a desert'.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 desert 的分词与形容词，意为「人已离去」，并非「像沙漠」。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for abandoning a person, post or cause, formed with -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 抛弃人、岗位或事业的行为名词，由 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: In the phrase just deserts, the word is the plural of deserve, not of desert; it means deserved punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 在 just deserts 这一短语中，它是 deserve 的复数，而非 desert 的复数，意为应得的惩罚。

entries.definition: Land that cannot be farmed or built on; it stresses uselessness rather than lack of rain.
entries.definitionCN: 无法耕作或建屋的土地；强调无用，而非缺雨。

entries.definition: Uncultivated land left to nature; it can be wet and fertile, so it is not a desert.
entries.definitionCN: 留给自然的未耕地；可以湿润肥沃，因此不是沙漠。

entries.definition: Poor, often stony ground that bears little; it may receive normal rainfall.
entries.definitionCN: 贫瘠、多石的薄地；降水可能正常。

entries.definition: Farmland turned to blowing dust by drought and bad practice; it is a human-made disaster, not a climate zone.
entries.definitionCN: 因干旱与错误耕作而变成扬尘的农田；是人为灾害，不是气候带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'un-' + serere 'bind': to desert is to break a tie.
normal.cn: de-「解除」+ serere「联结」：desert 就是扯断纽带。

normal.en: Pronunciation splits the pair: /ˈdezət/ noun, /dɪˈzɜːt/ verb.
normal.cn: 读音分开两名：名词 /ˈdezət/，动词 /dɪˈzɜːt/。

normal.en: The family runs desert, deserted, desertion, deserter, desertification.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 desert、deserted、desertion、deserter、desertification。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: desert climate, desert plant, desert island, desert one's post.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：沙漠气候、荒漠植物、荒岛、擅离岗位。

normal.en: Spelling trap: one s is dry land, two s is cake.
normal.cn: 拼写陷阱：一个 s 是旱地，两个 s 是蛋糕。

abstract.en: Think of a knot being cut, and the two ends drifting apart.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结被剪断，两端各自漂开。

abstract.en: Think of a room emptied of people but still full of furniture.
abstract.cn: 想象一间人已走空、家具仍在的屋子。

abstract.en: Think of a place where even loyalty dries up and blows away.
abstract.cn: 想象一个连忠诚都干涸、被风吹走的地方。

examples.en: The desert receives less rain in a year than a city gets in a storm.
examples.cn: 这片荒漠一年的降水还不如城市一场暴雨多。

examples.en: No one should desert a friend in trouble.
examples.cn: 谁都不该在朋友有难时抛弃他。

examples.en: The village was deserted after the mine closed.
examples.cn: 矿场关闭后，村庄空无一人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「desert」谐音「得晒特」——特别晒、特别干的地方 → 沙漠；动词读重音在后，意为「抛下」

root: 拉丁 serere「连接、编织」→ de- + serere = deserere「解开联结、抛弃」→ 分词 desertum「被弃置之地」→ 古法语 desert → 英语 desert。名词与动词同源；just deserts 的 deserts 另出来自 deserve。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split cleanly: four describe a dry, empty or barren place, four describe the act of abandoning a person, post, place or cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分成两半：四个描述干旱、空无或荒凉之地，四个描述抛弃人、岗位、地方或事业的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken bond, whether between people or between land and its use.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被扯断的纽带，无论在人之间，还是土地与用途之间。

branches.en: PHYSICAL DRYNESS: abandoned land becomes sand sea, stony plain or cold waste.
branches.cn: 物理干旱：被弃置的土地变成沙海、砾漠或寒冷荒地。

branches.en: EMPTINESS: a place can be empty of life, of culture or of people.
branches.cn: 空无：一个地方可以没有生命、没有文化，也可以没有人。

branches.en: PERSON: the first abandonment is leaving someone who relied on you.
branches.cn: 人：最初的抛弃是离开依赖你的人。

branches.en: DUTY: military law turns abandonment into a named offence.
branches.cn: 职守：军事法把抛弃变成有专名的罪名。

branches.en: ALLEGIANCE: the last abandonment leaves no object behind, only withdrawn support.
branches.cn: 效忠：最后的抛弃不留下对象，只留下撤回的支持。

intro.en: Desert is a Latin participle that English uses as noun, verb and adjective; its family is built with -ed, -ion, -er and -ification.
intro.cn: desert 是拉丁分词，英语把它用作名词、动词与形容词；其词族由 -ed、-ion、-er、-ification 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin line is serere 'bind' → deserere 'abandon' → desertum 'abandoned place', which gives the English noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁线索是 serere「联结」→ deserere「抛弃」→ desertum「被弃置之地」，由此产生英语名词与动词。

items.example: The prefix reverses the tying of a bond.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀反转了纽带的系结。

items.example: The root image is weaving strands together.
items.exampleCN: 词根意象是把股线编在一起。

items.example: To desert is literally to unbind.
items.exampleCN: desert 字面上就是「解开捆绑」。

items.example: The noun and verb split by pronunciation.
items.exampleCN: 名词与动词靠读音分开。

items.example: The deserted street had no lights.
items.exampleCN: 空无一人的街道没有灯。

items.example: Desertion in wartime is a serious charge.
items.exampleCN: 战时擅离是重罪。

items.example: The deserter was caught at the border.
items.exampleCN: 逃兵在边境被捕。

items.example: Overgrazing speeds desertification.
items.exampleCN: 过牧加速荒漠化。

definition_zh: 荒漠化；土地退化（干旱、半干旱与半湿润偏旱地区变成荒漠或类似荒漠）
definition_en: the process by which fertile land in dry regions becomes desert or desert-like through degradation
core_image: 曾经放牧的草坡上，表土被风刮走，砾石露出来，沙丘从北边一寸寸压过来
scene: 北边的沙丘一寸寸压过来，过牧与地下水位下降让整片牧地失去生产力。Overgrazing and a falling water table have driven desertification across the northern rangelands.
sceneCN: 这里 desertification 指「干旱地区土地退化为荒漠或类似荒漠的过程」（第 1 个义项：干燥区土地退化）；句意为过牧与地下水位下降，使北部牧地全面荒漠化。图中可辨识物件：裸露砾石、压来的沙丘、枯草根、下沉的水井。

pos.zh: 荒漠化；土地荒漠化（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 使荒漠化；使退化为荒漠

senses.title: Land degradation in dry regions
senses.definition: the reduction of the productivity of dryland ecosystems through soil loss, salinization or vegetation decline
senses.definitionCN: 旱地生态系统因土壤流失、盐渍化或植被衰退而生产力下降
senses.example: Overgrazing and a falling water table have driven desertification across the northern rangelands.
senses.exampleCN: 过牧与地下水位下降，使北部牧地全面荒漠化。
senses.why: the word names a process of loss, not the mere presence of desert; the land was productive and is becoming less so.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是「失去」的过程，而非沙漠的存在本身；土地原本有生产力，正在变弱。

senses.title: Expansion of desert margins
senses.definition: the outward spread of sand and bare ground at the edge of an existing desert
senses.definitionCN: 现有荒漠边缘的沙地与裸地向外扩展
senses.example: Satellite images show the desert margin advancing a few kilometres a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星影像显示荒漠边缘每十年推进数公里。
senses.why: this is the popular reading, but scientists keep it separate: margins shift naturally, while desertification is about lost productivity.
senses.whyCN: 这是大众读法，但科学家把它分开：边缘会自然移动，而荒漠化讲的是生产力丧失。

senses.title: Caused by overgrazing and clearing
senses.titleCN: 由过牧与清除植被引起
senses.definition: desertification produced by too many animals, fuelwood cutting or forest clearance on fragile dryland soils
senses.definitionCN: 在脆弱旱地土壤上，因牲畜过多、砍薪或清除森林而造成的荒漠化
senses.example: Goat herds stripped the slopes, and desertification followed within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 山羊群把坡地啃光，十年内便出现荒漠化。
senses.why: the process is usually human-driven, so the word often carries a criticism of land use rather than a description of climate.
senses.whyCN: 这一过程通常由人驱动，因此这个词常带对土地利用的批评，而不只是描述气候。

senses.title: Salinization from poor irrigation
senses.titleCN: 不当灌溉造成的盐渍化
senses.definition: land turning barren when irrigation raises the water table and salts accumulate at the surface
senses.definitionCN: 灌溉抬高地下水位、盐分表聚，使土地变得贫瘠
senses.example: Decades of flood irrigation left a crust of salt and desertification in the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年漫灌在三角洲留下盐壳与荒漠化。
senses.why: in irrigated drylands the mechanism is salt, not drought, yet the outcome is the same loss of cover.
senses.whyCN: 在灌溉旱地，机制是盐而非干旱，但结果同样是覆盖丧失。

senses.title: The policy definition under the UNCCD
senses.titleCN: 《联合国防治荒漠化公约》的定义
senses.definition: the legal definition used by the UN Convention, covering arid, semi-arid and dry subhumid zones
senses.definitionCN: 联合国公约采用的法律定义，涵盖干旱、半干旱与半湿润偏旱区
senses.example: The convention defines desertification by zone, not by the presence of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 公约按气候带而非按有无沙来定义荒漠化。
senses.why: a treaty needed one measurable definition, so a scientific process became a legal category with boundaries.
senses.whyCN: 条约需要一个可测定义，于是科学过程变成有边界的法律类别。

senses.title: Its social and economic effects
senses.titleCN: 荒漠化的社会与经济后果
senses.definition: the loss of grazing and cropland that pushes rural people to migrate and raises food insecurity
senses.definitionCN: 牧场与农田丧失，迫使农村人口迁移并加剧粮食不安全
senses.example: Desertification in the Sahel is one driver of seasonal migration.
senses.exampleCN: 萨赫勒的荒漠化是季节性迁移的驱动因素之一。
senses.why: the word is used in development policy because the physical process has measurable human consequences.
senses.whyCN: 这个词用于发展政策，因为物理过程有可量度的人道后果。

senses.title: Combating it through land management
senses.titleCN: 通过土地管理加以防治
senses.definition: the set of practices, from rotation to terracing, that slow or reverse dryland degradation
senses.definitionCN: 从轮牧到梯田等一系列减缓或扭转旱地退化的做法
senses.example: Stone bunds and careful rotation have slowed desertification in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 石埂与精细轮牧减缓了村里的荒漠化。
senses.why: once the process is understood as human-made, it becomes something that can be combated rather than merely endured.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个过程被理解为人为，它就成了可以对抗、而非只能忍受的事。

senses.title: Monitoring and land degradation neutrality
senses.titleCN: 监测与土地退化零增长
senses.definition: the use of vegetation indices and land-cover data to track desertification and report against neutrality targets
senses.definitionCN: 用植被指数与土地覆盖数据追踪荒漠化，并对照零增长目标报告
senses.example: NDVI trends are used to report desertification under the neutrality target.
senses.exampleCN: 归一化植被指数趋势被用来报告零增长目标下的荒漠化。
senses.why: policy targets require numbers, so the process is now tracked as an index rather than described in words.
senses.whyCN: 政策目标需要数字，因此这一过程如今以指数追踪，而非用文字描述。

intro.en: Desertification is a twentieth-century coinage: desert plus -ification, from Latin facere 'to make'. The term was popularised by a French botanist in 1949.
intro.cn: desertification 是 20 世纪的新造词：desert 加 -ification，后者出自拉丁 facere「做、使」。该术语由一位法国植物学家在 1949 年推广。

items.en: Desertum 'abandoned place, waste' supplies the first element, through French desert.
items.cn: desertum「被弃置之地、荒地」经法语 desert 提供了第一个成分。

items.en: The suffix -ification goes back to Latin -ficatio, from facere 'to make, do', so the whole word means 'making into desert'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ification 上溯拉丁 -ficatio，出自 facere「做、使」，因此整词意为「使成为荒漠」。

items.en: French botanist Andre Aubreville used desertification in 1949 for the spread of desert conditions in the African tropics; English adopted it soon after.
items.cn: 法国植物学家安德烈·奥布雷维尔在 1949 年用 desertification 指非洲热带荒漠状况的扩展；英语随后采用。

items.en: The UN Conference on Desertification in 1977 gave the term global policy standing, and the 1994 convention fixed its legal definition.
items.cn: 1977 年联合国荒漠化会议使该术语获得全球政策地位，1994 年公约固定了其法律定义。

items.en: Source uncertain (scope): the coining is documented, but the boundary between reversible degradation and true desertification is still disputed, and the first English citation date is not exact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（适用范围）：造词有文献可查，但可逆退化与真正荒漠化的界线仍有争议，最早英语书证年代也不精确。

note.en: Group one separates the desert family and its look-alike; group two separates the processes that are often mistaken for desertification.
note.cn: 第一组区分 desert 词族及形近词；第二组区分常被误当作荒漠化的其他过程。

entries.definition: The process of dryland degradation, with the -ification suffix marking 'making into desert'.
entries.definitionCN: 旱地退化的过程，-ification 后缀标出「使成为荒漠」。

entries.definition: The removal of forest, which can contribute to desertification but is not the same process.
entries.definitionCN: 森林被清除，可促成荒漠化，但并非同一过程。

entries.definition: The resulting adjective for land that has undergone the process.
entries.definitionCN: 经历该过程之后土地的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make or become desert-like, formed by back-formation from desertification.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「使成为荒漠」的动词，由 desertification 逆构而成。

entries.definition: Any decline in land quality, including erosion and nutrient loss; desertification is its dryland form.
entries.definitionCN: 土地质量的任何下降，含侵蚀与养分丧失；荒漠化是其旱地形式。

entries.definition: A temporary rainfall deficit; repeated droughts can trigger desertification but are not the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 暂时的降水亏缺；反复干旱可触发荒漠化，但本身不是该过程。

entries.definition: Accumulation of salt in soil, often from irrigation; it is one pathway to desertification.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤盐分累积，常由灌溉引起；是荒漠化的一条路径。

entries.definition: The removal of topsoil by wind or water; a common driver rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 表土被风或水带走；是常见驱动因素，而非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: desert + -ification: the process of being made into desert.
normal.cn: desert + -ification：被造成荒漠的过程。

normal.en: Latin facere 'make' hides inside -ification.
normal.cn: -ification 里藏着拉丁 facere「做、使」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: combat desertification, desertification control, desertification monitoring.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：防治荒漠化、荒漠化治理、荒漠化监测。

normal.en: It is a process of lost productivity, not simply advancing sand.
normal.cn: 它是生产力丧失的过程，不只是沙在前进。

normal.en: The image is a grazed slope losing its soil to wind while dunes press from the north.
normal.cn: 意象是过牧的坡地土壤被风刮走，北边沙丘压来。

abstract.en: Think of a bank account drained not by one theft but by daily small withdrawals.
abstract.cn: 想象一个账户不是被一次偷空，而是被每天的小额支取掏干。

abstract.en: Think of a carpet worn through where everyone walks, not where the fire was.
abstract.cn: 想象地毯不是在着火处烧穿，而是在人人踩踏处磨穿。

abstract.en: Think of a diagnosis that turns a landscape into a number on a report.
abstract.cn: 想象一个诊断把一片景观变成一个报告上的数字。

examples.en: Desertification threatens the grazing that supports the whole district.
examples.cn: 荒漠化威胁着支撑整个地区的放牧业。

examples.en: The project maps desertification risk from rainfall and soil data.
examples.cn: 该项目用降水与土壤数据绘制荒漠化风险图。

examples.en: Planting shelterbelts is one way to slow desertification.
examples.cn: 营造防护林带是减缓荒漠化的一种办法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「desert（沙漠）+ ification（变成）」——土地正在变成沙漠 → 荒漠化

root: desert（拉丁 desertum「被弃置之地」）+ -ification（拉丁 -ficatio，出自 facere「做、使」）→「使成为荒漠」。术语由法国植物学家 1949 年推广，1977 年进入联合国政策语境。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses track one process from its physical mechanism through its causes, legal definition, human cost, remedy and measurement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追踪同一个过程：从物理机制，到成因、法律定义、人的代价、补救与计量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: productive dry land slowly losing its soil, its water and its cover.
core.cn: 核心意象：有生产力的旱地一点点失去土壤、水与覆盖。

branches.en: PROCESS VERSUS PICTURE: degradation is the mechanism; advancing sand is only its visible edge.
branches.cn: 过程与画面：退化是机制，前进的沙只是它可见的边缘。

branches.en: CAUSES: too many animals, too little cover, or irrigation that leaves salt behind.
branches.cn: 成因：牲畜过多、覆盖过少，或灌溉留下盐分。

branches.en: LAW: a treaty fixes climatic zones and turns a process into a legal category.
branches.cn: 法律：条约固定气候带，把过程变成法律类别。

branches.en: HUMAN COST AND REMEDY: people migrate, and land management can slow the loss.
branches.cn: 人的代价与补救：人们迁移，而土地管理可减缓丧失。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: indices and neutrality targets replace description with reporting.
branches.cn: 计量：指数与零增长目标用报告取代描述。

intro.en: Desertification combines a Latin-derived noun with the productive suffix -ification, so the word reads as 'making into desert'.
intro.cn: desertification 由拉丁来源名词与能产后缀 -ification 组合，读作「使成为荒漠」。

latinIntro.en: Latin desertum supplies 'desert' and facere supplies the -fic- inside the suffix; both are documented, not reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 desertum 提供「荒漠」，facere 提供后缀中的 -fic-；两者都有文献，而非重构。

items.example: The desert edge moved north.
items.exampleCN: 荒漠边缘向北移动。

items.example: The suffix turns a state into a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把状态变成过程。

items.example: Poor irrigation can desertify a delta.
items.exampleCN: 不当灌溉能使三角洲荒漠化。

items.example: Desertified rangeland loses its grass.
items.exampleCN: 荒漠化的牧地失去草被。

items.example: Desertification is monitored by satellite.
items.exampleCN: 荒漠化靠卫星监测。

items.example: Desertification control begins with grazing limits.
items.exampleCN: 荒漠化治理从限制放牧开始。

items.example: The map shows desertification risk by district.
items.exampleCN: 地图按区显示荒漠化风险。

items.example: Desertification monitoring uses vegetation indices.
items.exampleCN: 荒漠化监测使用植被指数。

definition_zh: 干旱的；干燥的；荒芜的；（文风、话题）枯燥无味的；缺乏感情的
definition_en: having so little rain that few plants can grow; also dry and uninteresting in style or feeling
core_image: 裂成多边形的黏土上，一丛带刺灌木孤零零地立着，天空白得没有云
scene: 裂开的黏土与带刺灌丛覆盖着这片干旱的平原。Cracked clay and thorny scrub covered the arid plain.
sceneCN: 这里 arid 指「降雨极少、植物难以生长的」（第 1 个义项：干旱气候或地区）；句意为裂开的黏土与带刺灌丛覆盖着这片干旱的平原。图中可辨识物件：多边形干裂缝、带刺灌丛、白色天空、砾石。

pos.zh: 干旱的；干燥的；荒芜的；枯燥的；无感情的

senses.title: A climate of very low rainfall
senses.definition: describing a climate whose annual rainfall is too low to support rain-fed agriculture or continuous vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 形容年降水太低、无法支持雨养农业或连续植被的气候
senses.example: Cracked clay and thorny scrub covered the arid plain.
senses.exampleCN: 裂开的黏土与带刺灌丛覆盖着这片干旱的平原。
senses.why: arid enters English from Latin aridus 'dry, parched', whose root image is a surface dried out by sun.
senses.whyCN: arid 来自拉丁 aridus「干燥、烤干」，其词根意象是被太阳晒干的地表。

senses.title: Dry and barren ground
senses.definition: describing land that holds little moisture and bears few plants, whether or not it is officially a desert
senses.definitionCN: 形容蓄水少、植物稀少的地，无论是否正式算作荒漠
senses.example: Nothing will grow on that arid slope without irrigation.
senses.exampleCN: 那片干旱坡地不灌溉什么也长不出来。
senses.why: the adjective describes a condition of the ground, while desert is a place and desertification is a process.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述地面的状态，而 desert 是地方、desertification 是过程。

senses.title: Arid soil chemistry
senses.definition: soil low in organic matter, often alkaline, with salt or calcium carbonate layers near the surface
senses.definitionCN: 有机质低、常偏碱，表层附近有盐层或碳酸钙层的土壤
senses.example: Arid soil forms a hard caliche layer that roots cannot pass.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱土壤形成坚硬的钙积层，根穿不过去。
senses.why: little rain means little leaching, so salts and carbonates stay where they form.
senses.whyCN: 雨少意味着淋洗少，盐与碳酸盐就留在原处。

senses.title: Hyper-arid extremes
senses.definition: the most severe dryness class, where rain may not fall for years and life survives only in rare niches
senses.definitionCN: 最严重的干旱等级，可能多年无雨，生命只在极少数微生境中存活
senses.example: Parts of the Atacama are hyper-arid rather than merely arid.
senses.exampleCN: 阿塔卡马的部分地区属于超干旱，而不只是干旱。
senses.why: classification needs degrees, so arid gained a marked upper extreme with its own prefix.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要等级，于是 arid 加前缀形成标记出的上端。

senses.title: The semi-arid transition
senses.definition: the zone between arid and subhumid where rainfall supports grass but not closed forest
senses.definitionCN: 介于干旱与半湿润之间、降水足以长草却不足以成林的带
senses.example: Semi-arid country can flip from crop to dust within one season.
senses.exampleCN: 半干旱地区能在一个季节内从庄稼变成尘土。
senses.why: the prefix semi- marks the boundary where the adjective stops applying strictly, and that boundary is the fragile zone.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 semi- 标出该形容词不再严格适用的界线，而这条界线正是脆弱地带。

senses.title: Dry and dull in style
senses.definition: describing writing, speech or a subject that is dry, lifeless and without interest
senses.definitionCN: 形容文字、言谈或话题干瘪、无生气、引不起兴趣
senses.example: The report was accurate but arid, page after page of figures.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告准确却枯燥，一页接一页的数字。
senses.why: the metaphor borrows the physical sense: a text with no rain has no growth in it.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻借物理义：没有雨的文字里也长不出东西。

senses.title: Emotionally dry
senses.definition: describing a manner or relationship that shows no warmth, feeling or imaginative sympathy
senses.definitionCN: 形容态度或关系没有温度、感情或想象性的体谅
senses.example: An arid handshake ended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 一次毫无温度的握手结束了会面。
senses.why: the same dryness moves from land to people: nothing nourishing passes between them.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「干」从土地移到人身上：彼此之间没有任何滋养性的东西传递。

senses.title: Arid-zone ecology
senses.definition: the study and description of dryland communities, whose plants evade, resist or store scarce water
senses.definitionCN: 对旱地群落的研究与描述，其植物回避、抵抗或储存稀缺的水
senses.example: Arid-zone plants often carry waxy leaves and deep taproots.
senses.exampleCN: 旱区植物常具蜡质叶与深主根。
senses.why: as a compound modifier, arid labels a whole branch of ecology defined by water scarcity.
senses.whyCN: 作复合修饰语时，arid 标出以缺水为定义的一整个生态学分支。

intro.en: Arid comes straight from Latin aridus 'dry, parched', built on the verb arere 'to be dry', so its Latin line is short and well documented.
intro.cn: arid 直接来自拉丁 aridus「干燥、烤干」，由动词 arere「干燥」构成，其拉丁线索短且有文献。

items.en: Arere meant 'to be dry or parched'. It also underlies arefacere 'to dry up', seen in English arefaction.
items.cn: arere 意为「干燥、被烤干」。它也构成 arefacere「使干」，英语 arefaction 即由此来。

items.en: The adjective aridus described ground, air or a person dried out; it is the direct source of English arid.
items.cn: 形容词 aridus 描述被晒干的地、空气或人；它是英语 arid 的直接来源。

items.en: English took arid in the sixteenth century, at first in the physical sense of parched ground, with the figurative sense following later.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 arid，最初指物理上被烤干的地，比喻义随后出现。

items.en: Modern climatology fixed arid as a measurable zone, usually below about 250 mm of rain a year, and added semi- and hyper- grades.
items.cn: 现代气候学把 arid 固定为可测的带，通常年降水低于约 250 毫米，并加上 semi- 与 hyper- 等级。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin root): the Indo-European root commonly reconstructed as *as- 'to burn, glow' is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前词根）：通常重构的印欧词根 *as-「燃烧、发光」属重构形式；最早英语书证年代亦不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the arid family and its near spellings; group two separates the physical and figurative synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组区分 arid 词族与相近拼写；第二组区分物理义与比喻义的同义词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being arid, both climatic and stylistic.
entries.definitionCN: 表示干旱状态的名词，兼指气候与文风。

entries.definition: The adverb, usually in the figurative sense of speaking or writing without warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，通常用于说话或写作缺乏温度的比喻义。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym of aridity; it is correct but much less frequent.
entries.definitionCN: aridity 的较罕用同义词；正确但频率低得多。

entries.definition: Half-dry: the transition zone that is dry but not yet desert.
entries.definitionCN: 半干燥：干旱但尚未成荒漠的过渡带。

entries.definition: The plain word for lacking moisture; arid is its technical and often more severe counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缺水的日常词；arid 是它技术化、通常更严重的对应词。

entries.definition: Dried out to cracking, used of soil, lips or throat; it stresses visible damage.
entries.definitionCN: 干到开裂，用于土壤、嘴唇或喉咙；强调可见的损伤。

entries.definition: Unable to bear crops or young; it is about productivity, not rainfall.
entries.definitionCN: 不能产作物或后代；讲的是生产力，不是降水。

entries.definition: A place, not a quality; a desert is arid, but arid land need not be a desert.
entries.definitionCN: 是地方而非性质；荒漠必干旱，但干旱地不必是荒漠。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin arere 'be dry' → aridus → arid: the shortest possible line.
normal.cn: 拉丁 arere「干燥」→ aridus → arid：最短的一条线。

normal.en: The family runs arid, aridity, aridly, aridness, semi-arid.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 arid、aridity、aridly、aridness、semi-arid。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: arid climate, arid region, arid soil, semi-arid.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：干旱气候、干旱地区、干旱土壤、半干旱。

normal.en: The metaphor is the same dryness applied to prose and manners.
normal.cn: 比喻就是把同一种「干」用在文章与举止上。

normal.en: The image is cracked clay under a white sky with one thorn bush.
normal.cn: 意象是白空之下一片裂开的黏土，只有一丛刺灌。

abstract.en: Think of a sponge left in the sun until it is hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一块海绵被晒到发硬。

abstract.en: Think of a conversation where nothing green ever comes up.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话里始终长不出一点绿色。

abstract.en: Think of a page so dry that the words crack apart.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸干到字都裂开。

examples.en: Arid regions cover roughly a third of the land surface.
examples.cn: 干旱地区约占陆地表面的三分之一。

examples.en: The lecture was learned but arid.
examples.cn: 那场讲座很有学问，却枯燥无味。

examples.en: Arid air sucked the moisture from the washing.
examples.cn: 干燥的空气把洗过的衣物水分吸干了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a-rid」联想「啊，rid（去掉）了水」——水被晒没了 → 干旱的

root: 拉丁 arere「干燥、被烤干」→ 形容词 aridus「干燥的」→ 英语 arid。通常重构的印欧词根 *as-「燃烧、发光」属重构形式，并非定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses carry one dryness from climate and soil into extreme grades, then into style, feeling and the ecology that studies it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种「干」从气候与土壤，带到极端等级，再带到文风、感情与研究它的生态学。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface baked hard by sun with too little water to support growth.
core.cn: 核心意象：被太阳烤硬的地表，水少到长不出东西。

branches.en: CLIMATE GRADES: arid is a zone, and semi-arid marks where it fades.
branches.cn: 气候等级：arid 是一个带，semi-arid 标出它消退之处。

branches.en: SEVERITY: from barren ground to years without rain, the same quality deepens.
branches.cn: 强度：从贫瘠地面到多年无雨，同一种性质不断加深。

branches.en: SOIL AND FLORA: little leaching leaves salt, and plants evolve wax and deep roots.
branches.cn: 土壤与植物：淋洗少留下盐，植物演化出蜡质与深根。

branches.en: STYLE: a text without rain has no growth, so it is called arid.
branches.cn: 文风：没有雨的文字长不出东西，因此被称作「干」。

branches.en: FEELING: the same dryness reaches manners and relationships.
branches.cn: 感情：同一种「干」延伸到举止与关系。

intro.en: Arid is a Latin adjective stem that takes English noun and adverb suffixes, and a semi- prefix for the transition zone.
intro.cn: arid 是拉丁形容词词干，可接英语名词与副词后缀，并可用 semi- 前缀表示过渡带。

latinIntro.en: Latin arere 'be dry' and aridus 'dry' are both documented; the deeper Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 arere「干燥」与 aridus「干燥的」均有文献；更深的印欧词根属重构。

items.example: Arid ground cracks into polygons.
items.exampleCN: 干旱地面裂成多边形。

items.example: Aridity is measured by rainfall against evaporation.
items.exampleCN: 干旱度以降水和蒸发相比来衡量。

items.example: He answered aridly, without warmth.
items.exampleCN: 他干巴巴地回答，毫无温度。

items.example: The aridness of the air preserved the wood.
items.exampleCN: 空气干燥使木头得以保存。

items.example: Semi-arid grassland feeds cattle in good years.
items.exampleCN: 半干旱草原在好年景能养牛。

items.example: Hyper-arid deserts may go years without rain.
items.exampleCN: 超干旱荒漠可能多年无雨。

items.example: Arid-zone soils are thin in humus.
items.exampleCN: 旱区土壤腐殖质薄。

items.example: Arefaction follows once the marsh is drained.
items.exampleCN: 湿地排干后便出现干燥过程。

definition_zh: 干旱；干旱度；干燥；（文风、情感）枯燥、冷淡
definition_en: the condition of being extremely dry, measured as the balance between rainfall and water loss; also dryness of style or feeling
core_image: 一排雨量筒和一只蒸发皿立在空地上，两组读数相差很大，干旱程度就被写成一个数
scene: 雨量筒与蒸发皿给出同一个数字，用来表示这个流域的干旱程度。Rain gauges and evaporation pans give a single number for the aridity of the basin.
sceneCN: 这里 aridity 指「降水与蒸发之间的亏缺程度」（第 1 个义项：气候干旱度）；句意为雨量筒与蒸发皿共同给出一个数字，表示该流域的干旱程度。图中可辨识物件：雨量筒、蒸发皿、记录板、干裂地面。

pos.zh: 干旱；干旱度；干燥（不可数）

senses.title: Climatic dryness as a deficit
senses.definition: the condition of a climate in which potential water loss by evaporation exceeds precipitation over the year
senses.definitionCN: 全年蒸发造成的水分损失超过降水的气候状态
senses.example: Rain gauges and evaporation pans give a single number for the aridity of the basin.
senses.exampleCN: 雨量筒与蒸发皿共同给出一个数字，表示该流域的干旱程度。
senses.why: aridity is a relationship, not a quantity of rain alone: the same rainfall is wet in a cool place and dry in a hot one.
senses.whyCN: 干旱是一种关系，而不只是雨量：同样的雨在凉处算湿，在热处算干。

senses.title: The aridity index
senses.definition: a numerical ratio, commonly precipitation divided by potential evapotranspiration, used to classify dry climates
senses.definitionCN: 常用降水除以潜在蒸散量的比值，用于划分干旱气候
senses.example: An aridity index below 0.05 marks the hyper-arid zone.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱指数低于 0.05 标为超干旱带。
senses.why: once aridity is defined as a ratio, it becomes a number that maps and policy can use.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把干旱定义为比值，它就变成地图与政策可用的数字。

senses.title: Moisture deficit in soil and air
senses.titleCN: 土壤与空气的水分亏缺
senses.definition: the dryness of soil or air measured as the shortfall between what could be held and what is present
senses.definitionCN: 土壤或空气的干燥，以可持水量与实际含水量的差额衡量
senses.example: Soil aridity deepened as the organic matter wore away.
senses.exampleCN: 随着有机质流失，土壤干旱程度加深。
senses.why: the same noun covers the medium as well as the climate, because both are defined by a shortfall.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也覆盖介质本身，因为两者都由亏缺定义。

senses.title: A gradient of ecological harshness
senses.titleCN: 生态严酷度的干旱梯度
senses.definition: the ordering of sites from moist to extremely dry along which species composition and cover change
senses.definitionCN: 从湿润到极干的地点排序，物种组成与覆盖沿此改变
senses.example: Species richness falls steadily along the aridity gradient.
senses.exampleCN: 物种丰富度沿干旱梯度稳定下降。
senses.why: ecologists treat aridity as a continuous axis, so one noun describes a whole sequence of habitats.
senses.whyCN: 生态学者把干旱当作连续轴，因此一个名词描述一整串生境。

senses.title: Hydrological dryness of a catchment
senses.definition: the tendency of a catchment to yield little runoff because most rain is evaporated or stored
senses.definitionCN: 流域因大部分降水被蒸发或蓄住而产流很少的倾向
senses.example: High aridity keeps the river dry for most of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 高干旱度使这条河一年中大部分时间断流。
senses.why: water managers use aridity for the balance of a whole basin, not only for the air above it.
senses.whyCN: 水利管理者用干旱度描述整个流域的收支，而不只是其上方的空气。

senses.title: Dryness of style
senses.definition: a quality of writing or speech that is dull, unadorned and without imaginative life
senses.definitionCN: 文字或言谈乏味、无修饰、缺乏想象生气的性质
senses.example: The aridity of the prose made the evidence hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 行文枯燥，使证据难以跟上。
senses.why: the metaphor treats a text as ground: no rain, no growth, no colour.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把文本当作土地：没有雨，就没有生长与颜色。

senses.title: Emotional coldness
senses.definition: an absence of warmth, sympathy or feeling in a manner or relationship
senses.definitionCN: 态度或关系中缺少温度、同情或感情
senses.example: There was an aridity in his voice that discouraged questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他声音里有一种冷淡，让人不敢提问。
senses.why: dryness transfers from climate to temperament because both describe a place where nothing nourishing grows.
senses.whyCN: 「干」从气候转到性情，因为两者都描述长不出滋养之物的地方。

senses.title: A field barren of new ideas
senses.definition: the state of a subject or discipline that has stopped producing fresh work or interest
senses.definitionCN: 某学科或话题停止产生新成果或新趣味的状况
senses.example: Critics complained of the aridity of the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抱怨这场辩论贫乏无物。
senses.why: the abstract sense extends the metaphor once more: a field can be dry just as land can.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把比喻再推一层：领域也能像土地一样「干」。

intro.en: Aridity is the Latin abstract noun ariditas, from aridus 'dry' plus -itas '-ity'; English took it nearly unchanged in form.
intro.cn: aridity 就是拉丁抽象名词 ariditas，由 aridus「干燥」加 -itas「-ity」构成；英语几乎原样借入。

items.en: Arere 'to be dry' supplies the root; its participle aridus described parched ground or air.
items.cn: arere「干燥」提供词根；其分词 aridus 描述被烤干的地或空气。

items.en: Ariditas 'dryness' added -itas, the suffix that turns an adjective into a state noun, to aridus.
items.cn: ariditas「干燥」在 aridus 上加 -itas，即把形容词变成状态名词的后缀。

items.en: English uses aridity from the seventeenth century, at first for physical dryness and later for style.
items.cn: 英语自 17 世纪使用 aridity，最初指物理干燥，后来也指文风。

items.en: Twentieth-century climatology defined aridity quantitatively through precipitation and potential evapotranspiration.
items.cn: 20 世纪气候学用降水与潜在蒸散量对干旱度做定量定义。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin root and first date): the Indo-European root behind arere is reconstructed, not attested, and the earliest English citation is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前词根与首见年代）：arere 背后的印欧词根属重构而非有文献；最早英语书证年代不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the arid family; group two separates dryness words that are not climatic states.
note.cn: 第一组区分 arid 词族；第二组区分并非气候状态的「干」词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning dry or dull; aridity is the noun built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为干旱或枯燥的形容词；aridity 是由它构成的名词。

entries.definition: The adverb, most often used of speaking or writing without warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，最常用于说话或写作缺乏温度。

entries.definition: An English-formed doublet of aridity; it exists but is far less common.
entries.definitionCN: 英语自造的 aridity 双重形式；存在但远不常用。

entries.definition: The process of land becoming desert; aridity is the climatic condition, desertification the change.
entries.definitionCN: 土地变成荒漠的过程；aridity 是气候状态，desertification 是变化。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for lacking moisture; aridity is its technical, climate-scale form.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缺水的日常名词；aridity 是其技术化、气候尺度的形式。

entries.definition: A period of unusually low rainfall; aridity is the long-term condition that makes drought hurt.
entries.definitionCN: 一段异常少雨的时期；aridity 是使干旱造成伤害的长期状态。

entries.definition: The removal or loss of water from a body or material; a process, not a climate.
entries.definitionCN: 物体或材料失水的过程；不是气候。

entries.definition: The state of bearing nothing; it may result from aridity but can also come from poor soil or cold.
entries.definitionCN: 不产东西的状态；可能由干旱造成，也可由贫土或寒冷造成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: arid + -ity: the state of being dry.
normal.cn: arid + -ity：干燥的状态。

normal.en: Latin ariditas is the same word, only with Latin endings.
normal.cn: 拉丁 ariditas 就是同一个词，只换了拉丁词尾。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: aridity index, climatic aridity, aridity gradient.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：干旱指数、气候干旱度、干旱梯度。

normal.en: It is a ratio, not a rainfall total.
normal.cn: 它是一个比值，而不是降水总量。

normal.en: The image is a rain gauge beside an evaporation pan, their readings far apart.
normal.cn: 意象是雨量筒与蒸发皿并立，两个读数相差很远。

abstract.en: Think of a plant that loses more water than it can drink.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物失去的水多于它能喝到的水。

abstract.en: Think of a voice with no moisture in it at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一个完全不含水分的嗓音。

abstract.en: Think of a field of study where the wells have all run dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一个所有水井都已干涸的研究领域。

examples.en: Aridity in the region has increased by a fifth since 1980.
examples.cn: 该地区的干旱度自 1980 年以来增加了五分之一。

examples.en: The aridity of the air is why the meat dries so fast.
examples.cn: 空气干燥正是肉干得这么快的原因。

examples.en: His aridity made the interview feel like a form to be filled in.
examples.cn: 他的冷淡让采访像在填一张表格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「arid（干旱）+ ity（性质）」——干旱的性质 → 干旱度

root: 拉丁 arere「干燥」→ aridus「干燥的」→ ariditas「干燥（状态）」→ 英语 aridity。arere 背后的印欧词根属重构，并非有文献的形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat aridity first as a climate ratio, then as a soil and habitat condition, then as a quality of writing, feeling and whole disciplines.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先把 aridity 当作气候比值，再当作土壤与生境状态，最后当作文字、情感与整个学科的性质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gap between what water arrives and what the air can take away.
core.cn: 核心意象：到来的水与空气能带走的水之间的差额。

branches.en: MEASURE: deficit becomes a ratio, and the ratio becomes a zone on a map.
branches.cn: 计量：亏缺变成比值，比值又变成地图上的带。

branches.en: MEDIA: the same shortfall is read in soil, air and the yield of a whole catchment.
branches.cn: 介质：同一种亏缺可在土壤、空气与整个流域的产流中读出。

branches.en: GRADIENT: ecologists line habitats up from moist to extremely dry.
branches.cn: 梯度：生态学者把生境从湿润到极干排成一线。

branches.en: STYLE AND FEELING: writing and manners inherit the same absence of nourishment.
branches.cn: 文风与情感：文字与举止继承了同一种滋养的缺席。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: a whole field can be judged dry when it stops producing.
branches.cn: 学科：一个领域停止产出时，也可被判为「干」。

intro.en: Aridity is arid plus -ity, the suffix that turns an adjective into a state noun; the Latin equivalent is -itas.
intro.cn: aridity 是 arid 加 -ity，即把形容词变成状态名词的后缀；其拉丁对应是 -itas。

latinIntro.en: Latin ariditas is the direct model: aridus plus -itas, both documented forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ariditas 是直接范本：aridus 加 -itas，两者均有文献。

items.example: An arid basin loses most of its rain to evaporation.
items.exampleCN: 干旱流域的雨大部分被蒸发掉。

items.example: The suffix turns dry into dryness.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「干」变成「干燥」。

items.example: Aridity is mapped by index value.
items.exampleCN: 干旱度按指数值制图。

items.example: The aridity index fell below 0.2.
items.exampleCN: 干旱指数降到 0.2 以下。

items.example: Cover thins along the aridity gradient.
items.exampleCN: 覆盖沿干旱梯度变稀。

items.example: Climatic aridity sets the limit for rain-fed crops.
items.exampleCN: 气候干旱度设定雨养作物的上限。

items.example: Semi-aridity supports grass but not forest.
items.exampleCN: 半干旱状态能长草却长不了森林。

items.example: Hyper-aridity leaves bare rock and salt.
items.exampleCN: 超干旱只留下裸岩与盐。

definition_zh: 干旱；旱灾；长期缺雨；（资源、机会的）长期匮乏
definition_en: a prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall that causes water shortage; also a long scarcity of anything
core_image: 水库退成一片龟裂的泥滩，旧船坞悬在干岸上方，远处只剩一条细水
scene: 连续第三年缺雨，水库退成一片龟裂的泥滩。The reservoir shrank to cracked mud after the third year of drought.
sceneCN: 这里 drought 指「持续异常少雨、造成缺水的时期」（第 1 个义项：气象干旱）；句意为连续第三年干旱之后，水库缩成龟裂泥滩。图中可辨识物件：泥滩裂缝、悬空的旧船坞、细水线、岸边枯草。

pos.zh: 干旱；旱灾；长期匮乏（可数或不可数）

forms.label: 形容词（干旱的；干旱造成的）

senses.title: A long period of low rainfall
senses.definition: a prolonged period in which rainfall falls well below the normal for that place and season
senses.definitionCN: 降水明显低于该地与季节常值的持续时期
senses.example: The reservoir shrank to cracked mud after the third year of drought.
senses.exampleCN: 连续第三年干旱之后，水库缩成龟裂的泥滩。
senses.why: drought is defined against a local normal, so the same rainfall can be a drought in one place and a wet year in another.
senses.whyCN: 干旱是相对于当地常值定义的，同样的雨在一地算旱，在另一地算湿年。

senses.title: Agricultural drought
senses.definition: the soil-moisture shortfall that harms crops at their sensitive growth stages
senses.definitionCN: 在作物敏感生长期造成损害的土壤水分亏缺
senses.example: Rain fell in June, but an agricultural drought had already ruined the maize.
senses.exampleCN: 六月下了雨，但农业干旱早已毁掉玉米。
senses.why: rain that arrives after the critical stage does not undo the damage, so farms experience drought differently from weather stations.
senses.whyCN: 关键期之后才来的雨挽不回损失，因此农田所经历的干旱与气象站不同。

senses.title: Hydrological drought
senses.definition: the lagged shortage of streamflow, groundwater and reservoir storage after rainfall deficits
senses.definitionCN: 降水亏缺之后，河流流量、地下水与水库蓄水滞后出现的不足
senses.example: Hydrological drought persisted for two years after the rains returned.
senses.exampleCN: 雨回来后，水文干旱仍持续了两年。
senses.why: catchments store water, so rivers and wells record drought later and recover more slowly than the sky does.
senses.whyCN: 流域会蓄水，因此河流与水井记录干旱更晚，恢复也比天空更慢。

senses.title: Socioeconomic drought
senses.definition: the shortfall that appears when demand for water, food or power exceeds supply under dry conditions
senses.definitionCN: 干旱条件下，对水、食物或电力的需求超过供给所出现的短缺
senses.example: The city's socioeconomic drought hit when reservoirs failed and demand kept rising.
senses.exampleCN: 水库见底而需求仍在上升时，城市的社会经济干旱爆发。
senses.why: the shortage is produced by the balance of supply and demand, not by rainfall alone.
senses.whyCN: 短缺由供给与需求的平衡造成，而非仅由降水造成。

senses.title: A seasonal dry spell
senses.definition: the predictable dry season of a monsoon or Mediterranean climate, which farmers plan around
senses.definitionCN: 季风或地中海气候中可预期的旱季，农民据此安排耕作
senses.example: The seasonal drought lasts from November to April here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的季节性干旱从十一月持续到四月。
senses.why: a dry season is normal, so drought becomes a question of degree: longer or harder than the usual dry spell.
senses.whyCN: 旱季本身正常，因此干旱变成程度问题：比通常的旱段更长或更烈。

senses.title: A figurative scarcity of anything
senses.definition: a prolonged shortage of something other than water, such as goals, funding or talent
senses.definitionCN: 水以外事物的长期短缺，如进球、资金或人才
senses.example: The club ended a ten-year drought without a title.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部结束了十年无冠的荒。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers 'no rain for too long' to any supply that has dried up.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把「太久没下雨」移到任何已干涸的供给上。

senses.title: Classifying drought severity
senses.definition: the grading of drought by indices such as the Palmer index or the standardised precipitation index
senses.definitionCN: 用帕尔默指数或标准化降水指数等指标对干旱分等
senses.example: The state declared drought stage three after the index fell for six months.
senses.exampleCN: 指数连续六个月下降后，州里宣布三级干旱。
senses.why: management needs thresholds, so a continuous deficit is divided into discrete stages that trigger rules.
senses.whyCN: 管理需要阈值，于是连续的亏缺被分成可触发规则的离散阶段。

senses.title: Drought as a slow disaster
senses.definition: a natural hazard that develops slowly, spreads widely and does most of its damage through food and water systems
senses.definitionCN: 发展缓慢、范围广、主要经食物与水系统造成损害的自然灾害
senses.example: Drought kills more livestock than any single storm.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱杀死的牲畜多过任何一场单独的风暴。
senses.why: unlike a flood, drought has no clear start, which is exactly why it is under-reported as a disaster.
senses.whyCN: 与洪水不同，干旱没有明确起点，这正是它作为灾害被少报的原因。

intro.en: Drought is a native English word from Old English drugað 'dryness', built on a verb for drying, and related to dry.
intro.cn: drought 是英语本族词，来自古英语 drugað「干燥」，由表示「使干」的动词构成，并与 dry 同族。

items.en: Drugað meant 'dryness' and was formed from drugian 'to dry', a Germanic verb of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: drugað 意为「干燥」，由 drugian「使干」构成，后者是更深来源不确定的日耳曼动词。

items.en: The stock behind both drought and dry is usually reconstructed as *draugiz 'dry', a form not directly attested.
items.cn: drought 与 dry 背后的共同词干通常重构为 *draugiz「干燥」，这一形式没有直接书证。

items.en: Middle English kept the word with the -ght ending that also appears in daughter and night, and fixed it as the noun for dry weather.
items.cn: 中古英语保留这个词，并带上也见于 daughter、night 的 -ght 词尾，固定为指干旱天气的名词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century drought extended figuratively to any long shortage, as in a scoring drought.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，drought 比喻性地扩展到任何长期短缺，如「进球荒」。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the relation to dry is accepted, but the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction; the exact first citation of the figurative sense is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：与 dry 的关系被接受，但其日耳曼语之前词根属重构；比喻义的最早书证年代不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the drought family and near spellings; group two separates the shortage words that are not a period of low rain.
note.cn: 第一组区分 drought 词族与相近拼写；第二组区分并非「少雨时期」的短缺词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning prone to drought, used of soils or regions; it is rare in modern prose.
entries.definitionCN: 意为易旱的形容词，用于土壤或地区；现代书面语中少见。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective for lacking moisture; it shares the same Germanic stock as drought.
entries.definitionCN: 表示缺水的日常形容词；与 drought 共享同一日耳曼词干。

entries.definition: Describing a plant or variety that can resist drought damage, a compound built on the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容能抵抗干旱损害的植物或品种，由该名词构成的复合词。

entries.definition: Land degradation to desert; drought can trigger it, but it is a lasting change of land, not a period.
entries.definitionCN: 土地退化为荒漠；干旱可触发它，但它是土地的持久变化，不是一段时期。

entries.definition: A short run of dry weather; drought is longer and is measured against a local normal.
entries.definitionCN: 一段较短的干燥天气；干旱更长，并要对照当地常值。

entries.definition: The resulting lack of usable water; a drought is one of its causes, along with demand and leakage.
entries.definitionCN: 由此产生的可用水不足；干旱是原因之一，需求与漏损也会造成。

entries.definition: The long-term climatic dryness of a place; drought is a departure from that place's normal.
entries.definitionCN: 某地长期的气候干燥；干旱是对该地常值的偏离。

entries.definition: A general shortage of any resource; it is the wider category to which figurative drought belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 任何资源的普遍短缺；是比喻性 drought 所属的更大类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English drugað 'dryness' is the direct ancestor.
normal.cn: 古英语 drugað「干燥」是直接祖先。

normal.en: The family runs drought, droughty, drought-resistant, drought-stricken.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 drought、droughty、drought-resistant、drought-stricken。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: severe drought, prolonged drought, drought relief, break the drought.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：严重干旱、长期干旱、抗旱救济、结束干旱。

normal.en: Four kinds: meteorological, agricultural, hydrological, socioeconomic.
normal.cn: 四种类型：气象、农业、水文、社会经济。

normal.en: The image is a reservoir turned to cracked mud with an stranded jetty.
normal.cn: 意象是水库变成龟裂泥滩，船坞搁在干岸上。

abstract.en: Think of a clock that has stopped but nobody can say when.
abstract.cn: 想象一只停了的钟，谁也说不出是哪一刻停的。

abstract.en: Think of a team scoring no goals for a decade, and the word borrowed from weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一支球队十年不进球，于是借用了天气的词。

abstract.en: Think of a debt that grows while the rain is absent.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔在无雨时不断增长的债。

examples.en: The drought lasted four years and emptied every farm dam.
examples.cn: 这场干旱持续四年，抽干了每个农用蓄水池。

examples.en: Drought relief reached the district only in the second year.
examples.cn: 抗旱救济到第二年才抵达该区。

examples.en: The orchestra ended its drought of recordings with a new album.
examples.cn: 乐团以一张新专辑结束了长期的录音空白。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「drought」读音近「照特」——太阳特别照，雨一直不来 → 干旱

root: 古英语 drugað「干燥」← drugian「使干」，与 dry 同出日耳曼词干 *draugiz（重构形式）。更深词源不确定，无拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate the weather period from its soil, river, demand and seasonal forms, then extend it to any long scarcity and to disaster management.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把天气时期与其土壤、河流、需求、季节形式分开，再扩展到任何长期匮乏与灾害管理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a water body withdrawing and leaving its old shoreline exposed.
core.cn: 核心意象：水体退去，露出旧日的岸线。

branches.en: WEATHER: a deficit against local normal, whether unexpected or seasonal.
branches.cn: 天气：对当地常值的亏缺，无论突发还是季节性。

branches.en: DELAY: soil dries first, then rivers and wells record the loss later.
branches.cn: 延迟：土壤先干，河流与水井更晚记录损失。

branches.en: DEMAND: shortage appears where supply and use no longer balance.
branches.cn: 需求：供给与使用不再平衡之处，短缺才出现。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any supply can be said to have gone without rain.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何供给都可被说成「久未下雨」。

branches.en: GOVERNANCE: thresholds turn a slow process into stages, warnings and relief.
branches.cn: 治理：阈值把缓慢过程变成阶段、警报与救济。

intro.en: Drought is a native noun that forms compounds freely, especially with resistant and tolerant for plant breeding.
intro.cn: drought 是本族名词，可自由构成复合词，尤其与 resistant、tolerant 组合用于植物育种。

latinIntro.en: Drought has no Latin element; the -ant in resistant and tolerant is Latin-derived, but it belongs to those adjectives, not to drought.
latinIntro.cn: drought 没有拉丁成分；resistant 与 tolerant 中的 -ant 虽源自拉丁，却属于那两个形容词，而非 drought。

items.example: The drought broke in early autumn.
items.exampleCN: 干旱在初秋结束。

items.example: Droughty soils hold little water.
items.exampleCN: 易旱土壤蓄水少。

items.example: Drought-resistant millet survives on little rain.
items.exampleCN: 抗旱黍靠少量雨水存活。

items.example: Drought-tolerant shrubs suit dry gardens.
items.exampleCN: 耐旱灌木适合干旱庭园。

items.example: Drought-stricken villages relied on tankers.
items.exampleCN: 受旱村庄依靠运水车。

items.example: Drought-prone districts store fodder early.
items.exampleCN: 易旱区早早储备饲草。

items.example: In a drought year the wells fail first.
items.exampleCN: 干旱年里水井最先枯。

items.meaning: end a dry period or a long failure
items.example: The storm broke the drought at last.
items.exampleCN: 这场风暴终于结束了干旱。

definition_zh: 抗干旱的；抗旱的；在缺水条件下仍能保持产量或存活的
definition_en: able to withstand dry conditions without serious damage or loss of yield
core_image: 旱年里别的作物已经枯黄，一片黍子仍抽着穗，根扎得很深
scene: 旱年里别的作物已经枯黄，这片黍子却仍抽穗结实。Farmers here sow a drought-resistant millet that still fills the granary in a dry year.
sceneCN: 这里 drought-resistant 指「在缺水条件下仍能保持产量或存活」（第 1 个义项：抗旱作物品种）；句意为当地农民播种一种抗旱黍，旱年仍能装满粮仓。图中可辨识物件：抽穗的黍、旁边枯黄的作物、深根剖面、空水桶。

pos.zh: 抗干旱的；抗旱的（复合形容词）

forms.label: 同义复合形容词（耐旱的）

senses.title: A crop that yields under low water
senses.titleCN: 在缺水条件下仍能保持产量的作物
senses.definition: describing a crop variety that produces a usable harvest with far less water than usual
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种用远少于常规的水量仍能产出可用收成的作物品种
senses.example: Farmers here sow a drought-resistant millet that still fills the granary in a dry year.
senses.exampleCN: 当地农民播种一种抗旱黍，旱年仍能装满粮仓。
senses.why: the compound joins the hazard to the ability to resist it, so it names a performance under stress rather than a botanical category.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把灾害与抵抗能力连在一起，命名的是一种压力下的表现，而非植物学类别。

senses.title: A plant adapted to dry sites
senses.definition: describing a species with deep roots, waxy leaves or water storage that lets it live where rain is scarce
senses.definitionCN: 形容具深根、蜡质叶或储水结构、能在少雨处生存的物种
senses.example: Drought-resistant shrubs hold the sand around the well.
senses.exampleCN: 抗旱灌木固定住水井周围的沙。
senses.why: the word describes an outcome, while xerophyte names the mechanism; the two overlap but are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述结果，旱生植物命名机制；两者重叠但不可互换。

senses.title: A garden and landscape choice
senses.titleCN: 庭园与景观的选种标准
senses.definition: describing planting chosen so that beds survive on rainfall alone or with minimal irrigation
senses.definitionCN: 形容为使花坛仅靠降水或极少灌溉就能存活而选的植物
senses.example: The new border is entirely drought-resistant, with lavender and rosemary.
senses.exampleCN: 新花坛全用抗旱植物，种着薰衣草与迷迭香。
senses.why: water restrictions turned an agricultural trait into a design criterion for gardens and public parks.
senses.whyCN: 限水措施把农业性状变成了庭园与公园的设计标准。

senses.title: A breeding and genetic objective
senses.definition: describing a trait that breeders select for, often by crossing landraces with high-yielding lines
senses.definitionCN: 形容育种者选育的性状，常通过地方品种与高产品系杂交获得
senses.example: The programme released a drought-resistant sorghum after ten seasons of selection.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目经十个季节选育，释放出一个抗旱高粱品种。
senses.why: once a trait can be measured and inherited, it becomes a target in a breeding programme rather than a description of a plant.
senses.whyCN: 当性状可测量且可遗传，它就成了育种目标，而不只是对植物的描述。

senses.title: A turf and amenity grass cultivar
senses.definition: describing a turf grass bred to stay green with little watering, used on pitches and verges
senses.definitionCN: 形容育成的、少浇水也能保持绿色的草坪草，用于球场与路旁
senses.example: The council replaced the pitch with a drought-resistant turf.
senses.exampleCN: 议会把球场换成抗旱草坪。
senses.why: the same trait serves an ornamental and recreational market, where appearance matters more than yield.
senses.whyCN: 同一性状也服务于观赏与休闲市场，那里外观比产量更重要。

senses.title: A water system built for dry years
senses.titleCN: 为旱年设计的供水系统
senses.definition: describing infrastructure, such as storage or dual supply, that keeps working through a long dry period
senses.definitionCN: 形容能在长期干旱中继续运转的基础设施，如蓄水或双源供水
senses.example: A drought-resistant water supply needs more than one source.
senses.exampleCN: 抗旱供水需要不止一个水源。
senses.why: the compound escapes biology here: what resists drought is a system designed for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词在此走出生物学：抗干旱的是一个为此设计的系统。

senses.title: Figuratively resilient to scarcity
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：对长期匮乏有抵抗力
senses.definition: describing an economy, business or institution able to keep functioning when a key resource runs short
senses.definitionCN: 形容在关键资源短缺时仍能运转的经济、企业或机构
senses.example: The utility called its balance sheet drought-resistant after two dry years.
senses.exampleCN: 连续两个旱年之后，该公用事业称其资产负债表「抗旱」。
senses.why: the metaphor extends the agricultural trait to any system exposed to a prolonged shortage.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把农业性状扩展到任何暴露于长期短缺的系统。

senses.title: Distinct from drought-tolerant
senses.definition: describing the strategy of avoiding or resisting damage, as opposed to merely enduring lower yield
senses.definitionCN: 形容回避或抵抗损害的策略，而非仅仅忍受产量下降
senses.example: A drought-resistant line keeps its grain fill, while a tolerant one merely survives.
senses.exampleCN: 抗旱品系能保住灌浆，而耐旱品系只是活下来。
senses.why: resistance implies active defence, tolerance implies endurance, and breeders and ecologists keep the two apart.
senses.whyCN: 「抗」含主动防御，「耐」含忍受，育种者与生态学者把两者分开。

intro.en: Drought-resistant is an English compound of drought (Old English 'dryness') and resistant (from Latin resistere 'to stand against').
intro.cn: drought-resistant 是英语复合词：drought 出自古英语「干燥」，resistant 出自拉丁 resistere「站住对抗」。

items.en: Drought descends from drugað 'dryness', from drugian 'to dry', a Germanic word of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: drought 出自 drugað「干燥」，源于 drugian「使干」，是更深来源不确定的日耳曼词。

items.en: Resistant contains Latin sistere 'to stand, stop', from stare 'to stand'; the image is holding one's ground.
items.cn: resistant 含拉丁 sistere「站住、停住」，出自 stare「站立」；意象是守住阵地。

items.en: Re- 'against' plus sistere gave resistere 'to withstand, oppose', the direct source of resist and resistant.
items.cn: re-「对抗」加 sistere 构成 resistere「抵抗、顶住」，是 resist 与 resistant 的直接来源。

items.en: The hyphenated compound drought-resistant is a twentieth-century formation, driven by plant breeding and water management.
items.cn: 带连字符的复合词 drought-resistant 是 20 世纪的形成，由植物育种与水资源管理推动。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the compound's earliest written use is not securely dated, and the pre-Germanic root of drought remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个复合词的最早书面使用年代不可靠；drought 的日耳曼语之前词根仍属重构。

note.en: Group one separates the drought- compounds that differ by the second element; group two gives the wider vocabulary of hardiness.
note.cn: 第一组区分第二个成分不同的 drought- 复合词；第二组给出「耐受」的更大词族。

entries.definition: Able to endure dry conditions with reduced growth; it stresses survival rather than maintained yield.
entries.definitionCN: 能在干旱条件下以降低生长为代价存活；强调活下来，而非保住产量。

entries.definition: A plainer, often horticultural term for plants that come through drought unharmed.
entries.definitionCN: 更通俗、常用于园艺的术语，指安然度过干旱的植物。

entries.definition: Claiming complete protection from drought; it is a strong word rarely justified by evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 声称完全不受干旱影响；语气很强，证据上很少站得住。

entries.definition: Resistant to water damage rather than to lack of water; the same suffix, the opposite condition.
entries.definitionCN: 抗水损害而非抗缺水；同一后缀，条件相反。

entries.definition: Able to survive harsh conditions generally, including cold; it is broader than drought-resistant.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指能熬过严酷条件，包括寒冷；比 drought-resistant 宽。

entries.definition: Able to recover after damage; drought resistance is about avoiding damage in the first place.
entries.definitionCN: 受损后能恢复；抗旱性讲的是首先避免受损。

entries.definition: Describing plants structurally adapted to dry habitats; a technical term for the mechanism, not the outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 描述在结构上适应干旱生境的植物；是机制的技术术语，而非结果。

entries.definition: Able to endure a stress without dying; it says nothing about keeping full performance.
entries.definitionCN: 能忍受某种压力而不死；并不表示能保持全部表现。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: drought + resistant: the hazard plus the ability to stand against it.
normal.cn: drought + resistant：灾害加上顶住它的能力。

normal.en: Latin sistere 'stand' is inside resistant: to resist is to hold one's ground.
normal.cn: resistant 里有拉丁 sistere「站立」：抵抗就是守住阵地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: drought-resistant crop, variety, turf, water supply.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：抗旱作物、抗旱品种、抗旱草坪、抗旱供水。

normal.en: The noun is drought resistance, not drought-resistantness.
normal.cn: 名词是 drought resistance，而不是 drought-resistantness。

normal.en: The image is millet standing green while neighbouring crops have wilted.
normal.cn: 意象是黍子仍绿，旁边作物已枯。

abstract.en: Think of a plant that keeps its purse closed when water is scarce.
abstract.cn: 想象一株在水少时把钱包捂紧的植物。

abstract.en: Think of a town with two wells instead of one.
abstract.cn: 想象一座有两口井而不是一口井的城镇。

abstract.en: Think of a boxer who stays on his feet rather than merely surviving the round.
abstract.cn: 想象一名拳手是站稳脚跟，而不只是熬过这一回合。

examples.en: Drought-resistant varieties buy farmers one extra month of growth.
examples.cn: 抗旱品种为农民多争取一个月的生长期。

examples.en: The garden was replanted with drought-resistant species after the hosepipe ban.
examples.cn: 限用软管浇水后，庭园改种了抗旱物种。

examples.en: No crop is truly drought-proof, only more or less resistant.
examples.cn: 没有作物真正完全抗旱，只有抗性强弱之别。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「drought（干旱）+ resistant（抵抗的）」——能抵抗干旱的 → 抗旱的

root: drought（古英语 drugað「干燥」，日耳曼词，更深来源不确定）+ resistant（拉丁 resistere「抵抗」= re- + sistere「站住」）。英语复合形容词，19-20 世纪形成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one ability to crops, wild plants, gardens, breeding programmes, turf, water systems and even balance sheets.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一种能力用于作物、野生植物、庭园、育种计划、草坪、供水系统，甚至资产负债表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plant holding its ground and its grain while the ground around it dries.
core.cn: 核心意象：周围地面在干，植物却守住阵地与收成。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: the trait is read as yield under stress and as structure suited to dry sites.
branches.cn: 生物学：这一性状既读作压力下的产量，也读作适应旱地的结构。

branches.en: HORTICULTURE: the same trait becomes a planting choice for beds and pitches.
branches.cn: 园艺：同一性状成为花坛与球场的选种标准。

branches.en: BREEDING: once measurable, resistance becomes a selection target.
branches.cn: 育种：一旦可测，抗性就成为选育目标。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: water networks and balance sheets can also be called resistant.
branches.cn: 系统：供水网络与资产负债表也可被称为「抗旱」。

branches.en: DEFINITION: resistance is active defence, tolerance mere endurance.
branches.cn: 界定：「抗性」是主动防御，「耐性」只是忍受。

intro.en: Drought-resistant is a two-part compound: a native noun plus a Latin-derived adjective ending in -ant.
intro.cn: drought-resistant 是两部分复合：本族名词加带 -ant 的拉丁来源形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin line belongs to the second element only: sistere 'stand' → resistere 'withstand' → resistant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁线索只属于第二个成分：sistere「站立」→ resistere「抵抗」→ resistant。

items.example: The drought lasted three years.
items.exampleCN: 干旱持续三年。

items.example: The variety resists lodging in wind.
items.exampleCN: 该品种抗风不倒伏。

items.example: The suffix makes resistant an adjective of ability.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀使 resistant 成为表能力的形容词。

items.example: Drought-resistant seed costs more but fails less.
items.exampleCN: 抗旱种子更贵，但失败更少。

items.example: Drought resistance is scored in field trials.
items.exampleCN: 抗旱性在田间试验中打分。

items.example: Drought-tolerant lines survive but yield less.
items.exampleCN: 耐旱品系能活，但产量较低。

items.example: Drought-hardy perennials suit dry borders.
items.exampleCN: 耐旱多年生植物适合干燥花坛。

items.example: Drought-stricken farms need fodder aid.
items.exampleCN: 受旱农场需要饲草援助。

definition_zh: 湿地；常年或季节性积水、土壤饱和的土地
definition_en: land that is saturated or covered by water for at least part of the year, supporting water-adapted plants
core_image: 芦苇立在浅水里，水面映着天光，水下的泥是黑的，边上就是城镇的排水口
scene: 芦苇立在浅水中，水面映着天光，这片湿地正过滤城镇的径流。Reeds stood in standing water across the wetland that filters the town's runoff.
sceneCN: 这里 wetland 指「常年或季节性积水、土壤饱和的土地」（第 1 个义项：湿地）；句意为芦苇立在浅水里，这片湿地正过滤城镇的径流。图中可辨识物件：芦苇、浅水、黑色泥底、排水口、水面倒影。

pos.zh: 湿地（可数或不可数）

collocations.zh: 拉姆萨尔湿地（国际重要湿地）

senses.title: Land saturated or covered by water
senses.titleCN: 积水或土壤饱和的土地
senses.definition: ground where water stands at or near the surface for long enough each year to shape the soil and the plants
senses.definitionCN: 水每年在表面或近表面停留足够久、从而塑造土壤与植物的地面
senses.example: Reeds stood in standing water across the wetland that filters the town's runoff.
senses.exampleCN: 芦苇立在浅水里，这片湿地正过滤城镇的径流。
senses.why: wet plus land names ground by its water condition, the same way woodland is named by trees.
senses.whyCN: wet 加 land 按水分条件给土地命名，正如 woodland 按树命名。

senses.title: The legal Ramsar definition
senses.titleCN: 拉姆萨尔公约的法律定义
senses.definition: the treaty definition covering marshes, fens, bogs, peatlands and shallow water, natural or artificial, permanent or temporary
senses.definitionCN: 公约定义，涵盖沼泽、矿质沼泽、泥炭沼泽与浅水，天然或人工、永久或暂时
senses.example: The treaty counts a seasonal salt pan as a wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 公约把季节性盐沼也算作湿地。
senses.why: a treaty needed one broad definition, so the word expanded from wet ground to a list of habitat types.
senses.whyCN: 条约需要一个宽泛定义，于是这个词从「湿的地」扩展为一串生境类型。

senses.title: Marsh, swamp, bog and fen types
senses.titleCN: 沼泽、木本沼泽、泥炭沼与矿质沼泽
senses.definition: the main wetland classes, separated by water chemistry, peat depth and whether trees or reeds dominate
senses.definitionCN: 主要湿地类别，按水化学、泥炭厚度与乔木或芦苇占优来区分
senses.example: A fen is fed by groundwater, while a bog is fed only by rain.
senses.exampleCN: 矿质沼泽由地下水补给，泥炭沼只靠雨水补给。
senses.why: one general word needed subdivisions, and each subtype carries its own water source and chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 一个总称需要细分，而每个亚型都有自己的水源与化学。

senses.title: Wetland functions and services
senses.titleCN: 湿地的功能与生态服务
senses.definition: the flood storage, sediment trapping, nutrient filtering and carbon burial that wet ground performs
senses.definitionCN: 湿地进行蓄洪、拦沙、过滤养分与埋藏碳的功能
senses.example: The wetland held back the flood peak for six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这片湿地把洪峰拦住了六个小时。
senses.why: policy began to value wetlands for what they do, not only for what they are.
senses.whyCN: 政策开始重视湿地「做什么」，而不只是「是什么」。

senses.title: A constructed wetland for treatment
senses.titleCN: 用于污水处理的工程湿地
senses.definition: an engineered bed of gravel, soil and reeds designed to clean wastewater as it passes through
senses.definitionCN: 由砾石、土壤与芦苇构成、使污水通过时得到净化的工程床
senses.example: The sewage works discharges into a constructed wetland before the river.
senses.exampleCN: 污水厂先把水排入人工湿地，再进入河流。
senses.why: the same word covers a built facility, because it reproduces the natural process on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指人工设施，因为它有意复制自然过程。

senses.title: Wetland restoration and conservation
senses.definition: the return of drained or filled ground to wet conditions, often by blocking ditches and reintroducing water
senses.definitionCN: 把排干或填埋的地恢复为湿生状态，常靠堵沟与重新引水
senses.example: Blocking the drains restored the wetland within three years.
senses.exampleCN: 堵住排水沟后，湿地在三年内恢复。
senses.why: conservation turned the cover word into a target, since most wetlands were lost by drainage.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作把这个覆盖词变成目标，因为多数湿地是被排干而失去的。

senses.title: Coastal wetlands
senses.definition: salt marshes, mangroves and tidal flats where fresh and salt water meet and tides set the rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 咸淡水交汇、潮汐定节奏的盐沼、红树林与潮滩
senses.example: The coastal wetland buffers the village from storm surge.
senses.exampleCN: 这片滨海湿地为村庄缓冲风暴潮。
senses.why: tides replace rainfall as the water source, so the same cover word takes a marine setting.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐取代降水成为水源，因此同一个覆盖词进入海洋环境。

senses.title: Wetland delineation for regulation
senses.titleCN: 法规中的湿地边界划定
senses.definition: the field test of hydric soil, water saturation and hydrophytic plants that fixes a legal boundary
senses.definitionCN: 以水成土、水分饱和与湿生植物三项现场指标确定法律边界
senses.example: The delineation found wetland inside the proposed building plot.
senses.exampleCN: 边界划定在拟建地块内发现了湿地。
senses.why: regulation needs a line on the ground, so the three criteria turn a habitat into a jurisdiction.
senses.whyCN: 法规需要地面上的一条线，于是三项指标把一个生境变成管辖范围。

intro.en: Wetland is a native English compound of wet and land, both Germanic; it became a standard term only in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: wetland 是 wet 与 land 构成的英语本族复合词，两者都属日耳曼语；到 20 世纪才成为标准术语。

items.en: Wæt meant 'wet, moist'. Its Germanic stock is usually reconstructed as *wataz, of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: wæt 意为「湿的」。其日耳曼词干通常重构为 *wataz，更深来源不确定。

items.en: Land meant 'ground, territory', from Germanic *landam, itself of unsettled pre-Germanic origin.
items.cn: land 意为「土地、领土」，出自日耳曼语 *landam，其在日耳曼语之前的来源无定论。

items.en: Wet land appears as plain description in nineteenth-century writing on drainage and agriculture.
items.cn: wet land 在 19 世纪关于排水与农业的写作中作为平实描述出现。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology and the 1971 Ramsar Convention fixed wetland as a single class covering marshes, bogs, fens and shallow water.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学与 1971 年拉姆萨尔公约把 wetland 固定为涵盖沼泽、泥炭沼、矿质沼泽与浅水的单一类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and root): the earliest use of the closed compound is not securely dated, and the deeper roots of wet and land are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根）：这个闭合复合词的最早使用年代不可靠；wet 与 land 的更深词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates the parallel -land cover compounds; group two separates the wetland types that are often used interchangeably.
note.cn: 第一组区分并列的 -land 覆盖复合词；第二组区分常被混用的湿地类型。

entries.definition: Land covered by trees; the defining factor is woody cover, not water.
entries.definitionCN: 树木覆盖的土地；决定因子是木本覆盖，不是水。

entries.definition: Land dominated by grass; it is usually well drained, the opposite condition to wetland.
entries.definitionCN: 以草为主的土地；通常排水良好，与湿地条件相反。

entries.definition: Land that depends on rainfall alone, without irrigation; it is the direct counterpart of wetland in agriculture.
entries.definitionCN: 仅靠降水、不灌溉的土地；在农业语境中是湿地的直接对照。

entries.definition: Land used for farming; it is a land-use class and can include drained former wetland.
entries.definitionCN: 用于农业的土地；是土地利用类别，可包含排干后的旧湿地。

entries.definition: Wetland dominated by grasses and reeds in shallow water; one type within the wider class.
entries.definitionCN: 浅水中以草与芦苇为主的湿地；是更大类别中的一种。

entries.definition: Wetland dominated by trees or shrubs, often with standing water; the woody counterpart of marsh.
entries.definitionCN: 以乔木或灌木为主、常有积水的湿地；是沼泽的木质对应型。

entries.definition: Acid peatland fed only by rain, with mosses and very low nutrient supply.
entries.definitionCN: 仅靠雨水补给的酸性泥炭地，长苔藓，养分极低。

entries.definition: Peatland fed by mineral-rich groundwater, so it is less acid and more fertile than a bog.
entries.definitionCN: 由富含矿物的地下水补给的泥炭地，比泥炭沼酸性低、更肥沃。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: wet + land: ground that stays wet long enough to change its soil and plants.
normal.cn: wet + land：湿得够久、足以改变土壤与植物的地。

normal.en: The family runs wet, wetness, wetland, dryland.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 wet、wetness、wetland、dryland。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: constructed wetland, coastal wetland, wetland restoration, wetland delineation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：人工湿地、滨海湿地、湿地恢复、湿地边界划定。

normal.en: Four main types: marsh, swamp, bog, fen.
normal.cn: 四个主要类型：marsh、swamp、bog、fen。

normal.en: The image is reeds in shallow water beside a town drain.
normal.cn: 意象是浅水中的芦苇，旁边是城镇排水口。

abstract.en: Think of a sponge that also serves as a filter and a nursery.
abstract.cn: 想象一块同时充当过滤器与育婴房的海绵。

abstract.en: Think of a boundary drawn not by a fence but by soil colour and plant roots.
abstract.cn: 想象一条不靠栅栏、而靠土色与植物根划出的边界。

abstract.en: Think of a place that is neither land nor water and is valuable for exactly that.
abstract.cn: 想象一个既非陆地也非水域的地方，而它的价值正来自这种中间性。

examples.en: Draining the wetland removed the village's natural flood defence.
examples.cn: 排干湿地使村庄失去了天然的防洪屏障。

examples.en: The constructed wetland removes nitrogen before the water reaches the lake.
examples.cn: 人工湿地在河水入湖前去除氮。

examples.en: Migrating cranes depend on a chain of shallow wetlands.
examples.cn: 迁徙的鹤依赖一连串浅水湿地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wet（湿）+ land（土地）」——长期湿着的土地 → 湿地

root: wet（古英语 wæt「湿的」，日耳曼语 *wataz 为重构）+ land（古英语 land「土地」，日耳曼语 *landam）。英语复合词，20 世纪成为科学与法律术语；无拉丁成分。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from wet ground itself to its legal definition, its types, its services, its built imitation, its restoration, its coastal form and its regulated boundary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从湿的地本身，走向法律定义、类型、服务、人工仿制、恢复、滨海形式与受管制的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ground where water decides what soil and plants can be.
core.cn: 核心意象：由水决定土壤与植物能怎样的地面。

branches.en: DEFINITION: wet ground becomes a treaty category covering many habitat types.
branches.cn: 定义：湿的地变成涵盖多种生境的条约类别。

branches.en: TYPES: water source and chemistry separate marsh, swamp, bog and fen.
branches.cn: 类型：水源与化学区分沼泽、木本沼泽、泥炭沼与矿质沼泽。

branches.en: WORK: the wetland stores floods and filters water, and engineers copy the process.
branches.cn: 工作：湿地蓄洪滤水，工程师复制这一过程。

branches.en: REPAIR AND COAST: drained ground can be rewetted, and tides create a marine version.
branches.cn: 修复与海岸：排干的地可重新蓄水，潮汐造出海洋版本。

branches.en: JURISDICTION: soil, water and plants draw a legal line on the ground.
branches.cn: 管辖：土壤、水与植物在地面上画出法律界线。

intro.en: Wetland is a native two-word compound; its family is small and built from wet rather than from prefixes.
intro.cn: wetland 是本族两词复合；其词族很小，且由 wet 派生，而非靠前缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in wetland; both halves are Germanic, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: wetland 没有拉丁成分；两半都属日耳曼语，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The path stayed wet all winter.
items.exampleCN: 小路整个冬天都是湿的。

items.example: The land lies below the high tide line.
items.exampleCN: 这块地低于高潮线。

items.example: The wetland fills every spring.
items.exampleCN: 这片湿地每年春天蓄满水。

items.example: Wetness decides which plants can root here.
items.exampleCN: 潮湿程度决定哪些植物能在此扎根。

items.example: The wetted margin stays green in August.
items.exampleCN: 被水浸润的边缘在八月仍绿。

items.example: Wetting the peat restarts the moss.
items.exampleCN: 润湿泥炭能让苔藓复苏。

items.example: Wetland restoration blocked the old drains.
items.exampleCN: 湿地恢复堵住了旧排水沟。

items.meaning: land without irrigation or standing water
items.example: Dryland farming depends on stored soil moisture.
items.exampleCN: 旱地农业依赖土壤蓄水。

definition_zh: 沼泽；湿地；盐沼；长着草与芦苇的浅水低地
definition_en: low-lying wet ground covered with grasses, reeds and soft mud, often flooded periodically
core_image: 潮水涨上来，芦苇只露出上半截，泥面被咸水没过，几条小水道在草间穿行
scene: 涨潮时，咸水漫过泥面，芦苇只露出半截。At high tide the marsh fills with brackish water and the reeds stand half submerged.
sceneCN: 这里 marsh 指「长着草与芦苇、周期性被水淹的低洼湿地」（第 1 个义项：草本沼泽）；句意为涨潮时咸水灌满沼泽，芦苇半没水中。图中可辨识物件：半没的芦苇、泥面、潮水线、弯曲小水道。

pos.zh: 沼泽；湿地；盐沼（可数或不可数）

forms.label: 形容词（沼泽的；多沼泽的）

derivatives.zh: 药蜀葵（棉花糖原名来源）

senses.title: Low wet ground with reeds and grass
senses.titleCN: 长着芦苇与草的低洼湿地
senses.definition: low-lying ground that is periodically flooded and carries grasses, reeds and soft mud rather than trees
senses.definitionCN: 周期性被淹、长草与芦苇、泥软而不长树的低洼地
senses.example: At high tide the marsh fills with brackish water and the reeds stand half submerged.
senses.exampleCN: 涨潮时咸水灌满沼泽，芦苇半没水中。
senses.why: marsh names wet ground by its soft, grassy cover, standing between open water and dry land.
senses.whyCN: marsh 按湿软、长草的覆盖来命名湿地，位于开阔水域与干地之间。

senses.title: Salt marsh at the coast
senses.definition: coastal wet ground flooded by tides, colonised by salt-tolerant grasses and cut by creeks
senses.definitionCN: 受潮汐淹没、由耐盐草类占据并被小水道切割的海岸湿地
senses.example: Salt marsh cordgrass traps sediment and builds the shore outward.
senses.exampleCN: 盐沼大米草拦住泥沙，把岸线向外造。
senses.why: the salt suffix marks the marine water source, which changes both the plants and the management.
senses.whyCN: salt 后缀标出海洋水源，这同时改变了植物与管理方式。

senses.title: Freshwater marsh inland
senses.definition: inland wetland fed by rain, streams or groundwater, with reeds, sedges and floating plants
senses.definitionCN: 由雨水、溪流或地下水补给的内陆湿地，长芦苇、莎草与浮水植物
senses.example: The freshwater marsh behind the dunes holds frogs all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 沙丘后的淡水沼泽整个夏天都有蛙。
senses.why: the same landform appears with fresh water, and the word covers both as long as the cover stays grassy.
senses.whyCN: 同样的地形也可由淡水形成；只要覆盖仍是草类，这个词两者都覆盖。

senses.title: Tidal creeks and the marsh platform
senses.definition: the marsh surface dissected by dendritic creeks that drain and refill with each tide
senses.definitionCN: 被树枝状潮沟切割、随每次潮汐排空与回灌的沼泽台面
senses.example: The marsh platform rises a few millimetres a year as sediment settles.
senses.exampleCN: 随着泥沙沉降，沼泽台面每年升高几毫米。
senses.why: marsh is not flat and static: its creeks and platform are built by the same tidal water that floods it.
senses.whyCN: 沼泽并非平坦静止：它的潮沟与台面正由淹没它的潮水造出。

senses.title: Habitat for waterbirds and amphibians
senses.titleCN: 水鸟与两栖动物的生境
senses.definition: the shallow, plant-rich wet ground used for nesting, feeding and shelter by birds, fish and amphibians
senses.definitionCN: 浅水、植物丰富的湿地，被鸟、鱼与两栖类用于筑巢、觅食与隐蔽
senses.example: The marsh hosts thousands of waders each migration.
senses.exampleCN: 每次迁徙，这片沼泽都接待成千上万的涉禽。
senses.why: the physical description becomes a habitat term once species are said to depend on it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦说某些物种依赖它，物理描述就变成生境术语。

senses.title: Drainage and reclamation
senses.definition: the historic conversion of marsh to farmland by ditches, pumps and embankments
senses.definitionCN: 历史上通过沟渠、抽水与堤坝把沼泽改为农田
senses.example: Reclamation turned the marsh into grazing land within two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 两代人之内，开垦就把沼泽变成牧场。
senses.why: the word carries a history of loss, because most European marsh was drained before it was valued.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着一段丧失史，因为欧洲多数沼泽在被重视之前就已排干。

senses.title: Marsh gas as methane
senses.definition: methane produced by decay under waterlogged, oxygen-poor conditions and released as bubbles
senses.definitionCN: 在积水缺氧条件下腐烂产生、以气泡释放的甲烷
senses.example: Marsh gas bubbled up when the spade broke the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 铁锹戳破泥面时，沼气冒了上来。
senses.why: the old name records an observable phenomenon before chemistry explained it.
senses.whyCN: 这个旧名记录了化学解释之前就能观察到的现象。

senses.title: Marsh as a mineral wetland class
senses.definition: in wetland classification, a mineral-soil wetland with grass or reed cover, as distinct from peat-forming bog and fen
senses.definitionCN: 湿地分类中，矿质土、以草或芦苇覆盖的湿地，区别于成泥炭的泥炭沼与矿质沼泽
senses.example: The survey separates marsh from fen by peat depth.
senses.exampleCN: 调查以泥炭厚度把沼泽与矿质沼泽分开。
senses.why: classification needs boundaries, so a common word is narrowed into a technical class defined by soil.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要边界，于是常用词被收窄为由土壤定义的技术类别。

intro.en: Marsh is a native Germanic word from Old English merisc, built on mere 'sea, lake'; Latin mare 'sea' is a cousin, not an ancestor.
intro.cn: marsh 是日耳曼本族词，来自古英语 merisc，由 mere「海、湖」构成；拉丁 mare「海」是远亲，而非祖先。

items.en: Merisc and mersc named marshy ground. The element mere meant 'sea, lake, pool', so the word began as 'water-land'.
items.cn: merisc 与 mersc 指沼泽地。其中 mere 意为「海、湖、池」，因此这个词原意是「水边的地」。

items.en: The Germanic stock is reconstructed as *marisk-, from *mari- 'sea, lake', a form not directly attested.
items.cn: 其日耳曼词干重构为 *marisk-，出自 *mari-「海、湖」，这一形式没有直接书证。

items.en: Latin mare 'sea' and English mere, marsh share the Indo-European root *mori- 'body of water'; they are cousins, not a borrowing.
items.cn: 拉丁 mare「海」与英语 mere、marsh 共享印欧词根 *mori-「水体」；它们是同源远亲，不是借词关系。

items.en: Middle English marsh kept both the wet ground and the plants cut from it; the place sense now dominates.
items.cn: 中古英语 marsh 兼指湿地与从其中割取的植物；如今地点义占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Germanic root *mori- is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：日耳曼语之前的词根 *mori- 属重构；最早英语书证年代不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates marsh from its own derivatives and compounds; group two separates the wetland types by water source and cover.
note.cn: 第一组区分 marsh 与其派生、复合词；第二组按水源与覆盖区分湿地类型。

entries.definition: Describing ground that is soft, wet and like a marsh; it is a quality, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容地面湿软如沼泽；是性质，不是地点。

entries.definition: Marsh considered as a stretch of land, often used in mapping and conservation.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一片土地的沼泽，常用于制图与保护。

entries.definition: The coastal, tide-flooded type written as one word in ecology; it is a narrower term than marsh.
entries.definitionCN: 生态学中连写的海岸潮汐型；比 marsh 窄。

entries.definition: A pink-flowered plant of salty marshes whose root once flavoured confectionery, hence marshmallow.
entries.definitionCN: 盐沼中开粉花的植物，其根曾用于调味糖果，marshmallow 即由此来。

entries.definition: Wetland dominated by trees or shrubs; marsh is the grassy, reed-dominated counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 以乔木或灌木为主的湿地；marsh 是以草与芦苇为主的对应型。

entries.definition: Acid peatland fed only by rain; it is organic and nutrient-poor, unlike a mineral marsh.
entries.definitionCN: 仅靠雨水补给的酸性泥炭地；有机质、养分贫乏，与矿质沼泽不同。

entries.definition: Peatland fed by mineral-rich groundwater; it may look grassy but builds peat.
entries.definitionCN: 由富矿物地下水补给的泥炭地；看似长草，却在造泥炭。

entries.definition: The general legal and scientific class that includes marsh, swamp, bog and fen.
entries.definitionCN: 包含 marsh、swamp、bog、fen 的通用法律与科学类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mere 'sea, lake' + -isc: the wet edge of water.
normal.cn: mere「海、湖」+ -isc：水的湿边缘。

normal.en: Latin mare 'sea' is a cousin through Indo-European *mori-, not a source.
normal.cn: 拉丁 mare「海」经印欧 *mori- 与之同源，是远亲，不是来源。

normal.en: The family runs marsh, marshy, marshland, saltmarsh, marsh mallow.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marsh、marshy、marshland、saltmarsh、marsh mallow。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: salt marsh, freshwater marsh, tidal marsh, marsh gas.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：盐沼、淡水沼泽、潮汐沼泽、沼气。

normal.en: The image is reeds half submerged as the tide comes in.
normal.cn: 意象是涨潮时半没水中的芦苇。

abstract.en: Think of a floor that is solid in winter and liquid in spring.
abstract.cn: 想象一块冬天坚硬、春天液化的地板。

abstract.en: Think of a border zone where neither land nor water can claim the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一块陆与水的边界带，两者都不能宣称拥有它。

abstract.en: Think of a place that smells of mud and keeps the memory of old floods.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带着泥味、记得旧日洪水的地方。

examples.en: The marsh floods every spring and dries to cracked mud by August.
examples.cn: 这片沼泽每年春天被淹，到八月干成裂泥。

examples.en: Mosquitoes breed in the stagnant edges of the marsh.
examples.cn: 蚊子在沼泽滞留的水边繁殖。

examples.en: The old marsh was drained to make the airport runway.
examples.cn: 旧沼泽被排干，用来修机场跑道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marsh」谐音「马什」——马踩下去陷住的湿软地 → 沼泽

root: 古英语 merisc / mersc「沼泽」← mere「海、湖」+ -isc。与拉丁 mare「海」同出印欧词根 *mori-「水体」，属同源远亲而非借用；*mori- 为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from grassy wet ground to its coastal and freshwater forms, its creeks, its wildlife, its drainage history, its gas and its technical class.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从长草的湿软地，走向海岸与淡水形式、潮沟、野生动物、排水史、沼气与技术分类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft ground at the edge of water, held by reeds.
core.cn: 核心意象：水边由芦苇固住的软地。

branches.en: BASE: soft wet ground with grassy cover, whether inland or fresh.
branches.cn: 基底：长草的湿软地，无论内陆还是淡水。

branches.en: SEA EDGE: tides flood it, cut creeks and build the platform upward.
branches.cn: 海缘：潮汐淹没它，切出潮沟，又把台面向上造。

branches.en: LIFE AND LOSS: it shelters wildlife, and it has been drained for farmland.
branches.cn: 生命与丧失：它庇护野生生物，也曾被排干为农田。

branches.en: DECAY: waterlogged mud without oxygen produces methane.
branches.cn: 腐烂：缺氧的积水泥产生甲烷。

branches.en: CLASS: mineral soil and grassy cover separate marsh from peatland.
branches.cn: 分类：矿质土与草覆盖把沼泽与泥炭地分开。

intro.en: Marsh is a native noun with a productive -y adjective and a land compound; its older element mere survives in place names.
intro.cn: marsh 是本族名词，可构成 -y 形容词与 land 复合词；其较古成分 mere 仍见于地名。

latinIntro.en: Latin mare is a cognate through Indo-European, not a source; it is listed for comparison, not as an ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mare 经印欧语与之同源，并非来源；列出仅供比较，不是祖先。

items.example: The marsh is grazed only in dry summers.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽只在干旱夏季放牧。

items.meaning: like a marsh, soft and wet
items.example: Marshy ground stopped the tractor.
items.exampleCN: 湿软的地陷住了拖拉机。

items.example: Marshland borders the estuary.
items.exampleCN: 沼泽地紧邻河口。

items.example: Saltmarsh sheep graze on the seaward grass.
items.exampleCN: 盐沼羊在向海的草地上吃草。

items.example: Marsh gas can burn when it collects in a drain.
items.exampleCN: 沼气在沟中积聚时可燃。

items.example: Marsh mallow root was once boiled for sweets.
items.exampleCN: 药蜀葵根曾用来熬制糖果。

items.meaning: a bird that nests in reeds
items.example: The marsh wren sings from a reed stem.
items.exampleCN: 沼泽苇莺在苇茎上鸣唱。

items.example: Mere survives in lake names such as Windermere.
items.exampleCN: mere 仍见于 Windermere 等湖名。
